-------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m6p2t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Seats, Students, Horizon

NoOne == "nobody"
Times == 0 .. Horizon

VARIABLES pool, leaseHolder, leaseExp, enrolledBy, clock
vars == <<pool, leaseHolder, leaseExp, enrolledBy, clock>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ pool \subseteq Seats
  /\ leaseHolder \in [Seats -> Students \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ leaseExp \in [Seats -> Times]
  /\ enrolledBy \in [Seats -> Students \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ clock \in Times

Init ==
  /\ pool = Seats
  /\ leaseHolder = [s \in Seats |-> NoOne]
  /\ leaseExp = [s \in Seats |-> 0]
  /\ enrolledBy = [s \in Seats |-> NoOne]
  /\ clock = 0

\* The registration clock is what makes a lease deadline meaningful.
Tick ==
  /\ clock < Horizon
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, leaseHolder, leaseExp, enrolledBy>>

\* A lease moves a seat out of the pool; the deadline is stamped from the clock.
OpenLease(s, st, d) ==
  /\ s \in pool
  /\ d \in Times
  /\ d >= clock
  /\ pool' = pool \ {s}
  /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![s] = st]
  /\ leaseExp' = [leaseExp EXCEPT ![s] = d]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolledBy, clock>>

ExpireLease(s) ==
  /\ leaseHolder[s] # NoOne
  /\ clock >= leaseExp[s]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {s}
  /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
  /\ leaseExp' = [leaseExp EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolledBy, clock>>

Confirm(s) ==
  /\ leaseHolder[s] # NoOne
  /\ clock < leaseExp[s]
  /\ enrolledBy' = [enrolledBy EXCEPT ![s] = leaseHolder[s]]
  /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
  /\ leaseExp' = [leaseExp EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, clock>>

Drop(s) ==
  /\ enrolledBy[s] # NoOne
  /\ enrolledBy' = [enrolledBy EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseHolder, leaseExp, clock>>

\* Registrar override: yanks a confirmed seat back without the student's help.
AdminRevoke(s) ==
  /\ enrolledBy[s] # NoOne
  /\ enrolledBy' = [enrolledBy EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {s}
  /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseExp, clock>>

Next ==
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E s \in Seats, st \in Students, d \in Times : OpenLease(s, st, d)
  \/ \E s \in Seats : ExpireLease(s)
  \/ \E s \in Seats : Confirm(s)
  \/ \E s \in Seats : Drop(s)
  \/ \E s \in Seats : AdminRevoke(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Custody coherence: each seat sits in exactly one of pool / lease / enrollment.
SeatCustodyExact ==
  /\ \A s \in Seats : (s \in pool) => (leaseHolder[s] = NoOne /\ enrolledBy[s] = NoOne)
  /\ \A s \in Seats : (leaseHolder[s] # NoOne) => (s \notin pool /\ enrolledBy[s] = NoOne)
  /\ \A s \in Seats : (enrolledBy[s] # NoOne) => (s \notin pool /\ leaseHolder[s] = NoOne)
  /\ \A s \in Seats : s \in pool \/ leaseHolder[s] # NoOne \/ enrolledBy[s] # NoOne
==========================================================================
nl:
A university course-registration system hands out seats in a single popular lecture course. Every seat in the course is a physical unit of capacity: it either sits unclaimed in the registrar's open pool, or it is held by a student under a short-lived reservation lease, or it has been turned into a confirmed enrollment. The registrar's accounting rule is that seats are never manufactured and never quietly vanish; a seat always sits in exactly one of those three places.

A student who wants a place takes a seat out of the open pool and receives a lease on it, stamped with an expiry deadline read off the registration clock. The clock advances on its own as the registration window runs. If a student lets the lease deadline pass without acting, the lease expires and the seat goes straight back into the open pool so somebody else can take it. If the student acts in time, the lease is converted into a confirmed enrollment and the lease record is torn up. A confirmed student may later drop the course, which releases the seat back into the open pool.

Because registration disputes happen, the system also carries a privileged registrar override: the registrar may administratively revoke a confirmed enrollment outright, without the student's cooperation, and the revoked seat is returned to the open pool exactly like a voluntary drop. The override bypasses the lease machinery entirely, which is precisely why the seat accounting has to be checked against it.

The full action set is: advance the registration clock, open a lease on a pooled seat for a student, expire a lease whose deadline has passed and return the seat to the pool, confirm a live lease into an enrollment, voluntarily drop a confirmed enrollment back to the pool, and the registrar's administrative revocation of a confirmed enrollment back to the pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every seat in the course is at all times in exactly one custody state -- unclaimed in the open pool, held under a lease, or confirmed as an enrollment -- so no seat is ever duplicated across two places and no seat ever disappears from the registrar's books.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od6m5p5t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Supervisors

NumCars == Cardinality(Cars)
Tickets == 0 .. NumCars

VARIABLES panel, ballot, phase, placard, issued
vars == <<panel, ballot, phase, placard, issued>>

\* A ballot carries only against the panel that is on duty right now, so the
\* threshold moves as supervisors join and leave mid-operation.
Carries(c) == /\ panel # {}
              /\ 2 * Cardinality(ballot[c] \cap panel) > Cardinality(panel)

TypeOK ==
  /\ panel \subseteq Supervisors
  /\ ballot \in [Cars -> SUBSET Supervisors]
  /\ phase \in [Cars -> {"idle", "armed", "recalled"}]
  /\ placard \in [Cars -> Tickets]
  /\ issued \in Tickets

Init ==
  /\ panel = Supervisors
  /\ ballot = [c \in Cars |-> {}]
  /\ phase = [c \in Cars |-> "idle"]
  /\ placard = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ issued = 0

ComeOnDuty(s) ==
  /\ s \notin panel
  /\ panel' = panel \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, phase, placard, issued>>

GoOffDuty(s) ==
  /\ s \in panel
  /\ panel' = panel \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, phase, placard, issued>>

CastVote(c, s) ==
  /\ s \in panel
  /\ phase[c] = "idle"
  /\ s \notin ballot[c]
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = ballot[c] \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<panel, phase, placard, issued>>

Arm(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "idle"
  /\ Carries(c)
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "armed"]
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<panel, placard, issued>>

\* Drawing the next sequential ticket is what makes a repeated recall visible:
\* a car that drew twice would abandon its first ticket, leaving a ledger gap.
Recall(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "armed"
  /\ issued < NumCars
  /\ issued' = issued + 1
  /\ placard' = [placard EXCEPT ![c] = issued + 1]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "recalled"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<panel, ballot>>

RecallAny == \E c \in Cars : Recall(c)

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Supervisors : ComeOnDuty(s)
  \/ \E s \in Supervisors : GoOffDuty(s)
  \/ \E c \in Cars, s \in Supervisors : CastVote(c, s)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Arm(c)
  \/ RecallAny

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(RecallAny)

\* Every issued ticket is still owned by some car's placard: gap-free ledger.
LedgerGapFree ==
  /\ \A c \in Cars : (phase[c] = "recalled") <=> (placard[c] # 0)
  /\ \A n \in 1 .. issued : \E c \in Cars : placard[c] = n

EveryArmedCarRecalled ==
  \A c \in Cars : (phase[c] = "armed") ~> (phase[c] = "recalled")
================================================================================
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank is watched by a rotating panel of on-duty safety supervisors. Supervisors go on and off duty continuously across shifts, so the size of the panel changes while the building is running, and every decision threshold is computed against whichever panel is on duty at that moment rather than against a fixed roster.

The bank's one irreversible action is the emergency fire recall of a car: the car is driven to the lobby, its doors are locked open, and its drive is physically cut. A recalled car cannot be returned to service by any operator; the cut is permanent. Because a recall strands passengers and takes a shaft out of the building's evacuation plan, it is never taken by a single supervisor. Each on-duty supervisor may cast a vote for recalling a particular car, and votes accumulate on that car's ballot. When the votes standing on a car's ballot from currently on-duty supervisors form a strict majority of the current on-duty panel, the ballot carries and the car is armed for recall; arming clears the ballot so the votes cannot be reused. Because the panel size moves, a ballot that does not yet carry may start carrying when supervisors go off duty, and a ballot that would have carried may stop carrying when new supervisors come on duty.

Every actual recall draws the next sequential recall ticket from the building's evacuation ledger. The ledger hands out ticket numbers 1, 2, 3, and so on, one per recall performed, and the ticket a car draws is written on that car's placard so the fire brigade can reconstruct the order in which shafts were taken out. An armed car is recalled by the bank controller, which is the step that draws the ticket and cuts the drive.

The full action set is: a supervisor comes on duty and joins the panel, a supervisor goes off duty and leaves the panel, an on-duty supervisor casts a vote on an idle car's recall ballot, an idle car whose ballot holds a strict majority of the on-duty panel is armed and its ballot cleared, and the controller recalls an armed car, drawing the next ledger ticket and cutting that car's drive.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The evacuation ledger stays gap-free in the sense that every ticket number the ledger has issued is written on some car's placard, which can only remain true if each car draws a ticket at most once, so no car is ever recalled twice.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every car that has been armed by a carrying ballot is eventually recalled by the controller.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m8p1t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Bins, HotBins, Instances, MaxTally

Free == "free"
NoBin == "nobin"
Cabinets == {"hot", "cold"}
CabinetOf(b) == IF b \in HotBins THEN "hot" ELSE "cold"
Tallies == 0 .. MaxTally

VARIABLES cabHeld, binHeld, tally, draftBin, draftSaw
vars == <<cabHeld, binHeld, tally, draftBin, draftSaw>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ cabHeld \in [Cabinets -> Instances \cup {Free}]
  /\ binHeld \in [Bins -> Instances \cup {Free}]
  /\ tally \in [Bins -> Tallies]
  /\ draftBin \in [Instances -> Bins \cup {NoBin}]
  /\ draftSaw \in [Instances -> Tallies]

Init ==
  /\ cabHeld = [k \in Cabinets |-> Free]
  /\ binHeld = [b \in Bins |-> Free]
  /\ tally = [b \in Bins |-> 0]
  /\ draftBin = [i \in Instances |-> NoBin]
  /\ draftSaw = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

TakeCabinet(i, k) ==
  /\ cabHeld[k] = Free
  /\ cabHeld' = [cabHeld EXCEPT ![k] = i]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<binHeld, tally, draftBin, draftSaw>>

\* Fine-grained hold is legal only under a cabinet the same instance already has.
TakeBin(i, b) ==
  /\ binHeld[b] = Free
  /\ cabHeld[CabinetOf(b)] = i
  /\ binHeld' = [binHeld EXCEPT ![b] = i]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabHeld, tally, draftBin, draftSaw>>

ReadDraft(i, b) ==
  /\ binHeld[b] = i
  /\ draftBin[i] = NoBin
  /\ draftBin' = [draftBin EXCEPT ![i] = b]
  /\ draftSaw' = [draftSaw EXCEPT ![i] = tally[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabHeld, binHeld, tally>>

\* Write-back stores saw+1; if the bin had moved on, that step erases the gap.
WriteBack(i) ==
  /\ draftBin[i] # NoBin
  /\ draftSaw[i] < MaxTally
  /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![draftBin[i]] = draftSaw[i] + 1]
  /\ draftBin' = [draftBin EXCEPT ![i] = NoBin]
  /\ draftSaw' = [draftSaw EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabHeld, binHeld>>

AbandonDraft(i) ==
  /\ draftBin[i] # NoBin
  /\ draftBin' = [draftBin EXCEPT ![i] = NoBin]
  /\ draftSaw' = [draftSaw EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabHeld, binHeld, tally>>

ReleaseBin(i, b) ==
  /\ binHeld[b] = i
  /\ draftBin[i] # b
  /\ binHeld' = [binHeld EXCEPT ![b] = Free]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabHeld, tally, draftBin, draftSaw>>

ReleaseCabinet(i, k) ==
  /\ cabHeld[k] = i
  /\ \A b \in Bins : CabinetOf(b) = k => binHeld[b] # i
  /\ cabHeld' = [cabHeld EXCEPT ![k] = Free]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<binHeld, tally, draftBin, draftSaw>>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances, k \in Cabinets : TakeCabinet(i, k)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Bins : TakeBin(i, b)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Bins : ReadDraft(i, b)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : WriteBack(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : AbandonDraft(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Bins : ReleaseBin(i, b)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, k \in Cabinets : ReleaseCabinet(i, k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Staleness check: an outstanding draft must still match the bin it came from.
NoStaleDraft ==
  \A i \in Instances :
    draftBin[i] # NoBin =>
      /\ binHeld[draftBin[i]] = i
      /\ draftSaw[i] = tally[draftBin[i]]
===========================================================================
nl:
A hospital pharmacy runs two independent prescription-dispenser instances, a main-floor unit and a satellite unit, that were installed by different vendors and never talk to each other directly. Both of them draw from one single physical stock pool: the same cabinets, the same bins, and the same per-bin dispensing record. Each bin's record holds a running dispense tally for that medication, and that tally is the shared record both instances read and write.

Access to the pool is arranged as a two-level hierarchy. Every bin lives inside a cabinet, and a dispenser instance may only take hold of a bin after it has first taken hold of the enclosing cabinet: coarse first, then fine. A cabinet may be held by only one instance at a time, and likewise a bin. An instance gives up a bin when it is finished with it, and gives up a cabinet only once it holds no bins inside that cabinet.

An update to a bin's tally is not atomic in this hardware. The instance first reads the bin's record into a local draft, noting the tally value it saw. Later, it writes the draft back, storing an incremented tally. Between the read and the write-back the instance is doing physical work -- counting tablets, printing a label -- so time passes. If the value in the bin had moved on since the draft was taken, writing the draft back would silently discard whatever happened in between; that is the lost update the hierarchy is there to prevent. An instance that decides not to finish may abandon its draft instead of writing it back.

The full action set is: an instance takes hold of a free cabinet, an instance takes hold of a free bin inside a cabinet it already holds, an instance reads a held bin's tally into a local draft, an instance writes a draft back to its bin as an incremented tally, an instance abandons a draft without writing it, an instance releases a bin it holds, and an instance releases a cabinet in which it holds no bins.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a dispenser instance is carrying an unwritten draft of a bin's tally, that draft's noted value still equals the bin's current tally and the instance still holds that bin, so no write-back can ever overwrite an update it did not see.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m0p2t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumBanks, TotalFunds, MaxAmount, StampCycle

Banks == 0 .. (NumBanks - 1)
NoPayee == NumBanks
Amounts == 0 .. MaxAmount
Money == 0 .. TotalFunds
Stamps == 0 .. (StampCycle - 1)

RECURSIVE SumOf(_, _)
SumOf(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOf(f, S \ {x})

VARIABLES balance, escrow, payee, stampSeen, stamp, agentAt
vars == <<balance, escrow, payee, stampSeen, stamp, agentAt>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ balance \in [Banks -> Money]
  /\ escrow \in [Banks -> Amounts]
  /\ payee \in [Banks -> Banks \cup {NoPayee}]
  /\ stampSeen \in [Banks -> Stamps]
  /\ stamp \in Stamps
  /\ agentAt \in Banks

Init ==
  /\ balance = [b \in Banks |-> IF b = 0 THEN TotalFunds ELSE 0]
  /\ escrow = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
  /\ payee = [b \in Banks |-> NoPayee]
  /\ stampSeen = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
  /\ stamp = 0
  /\ agentAt = 0

\* Optimistic origination: debit now, remember the stamp we drew against.
Originate(b, d, amt) ==
  /\ payee[b] = NoPayee
  /\ d # b
  /\ amt \in 1 .. MaxAmount
  /\ balance[b] >= amt
  /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![b] = balance[b] - amt]
  /\ escrow' = [escrow EXCEPT ![b] = amt]
  /\ payee' = [payee EXCEPT ![b] = d]
  /\ stampSeen' = [stampSeen EXCEPT ![b] = stamp]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, agentAt>>

\* Posting is the only writer of the shared stamp, which is what invalidates
\* every other participant's snapshot.
Post ==
  /\ payee[agentAt] # NoPayee
  /\ stampSeen[agentAt] = stamp
  /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![payee[agentAt]] = @ + escrow[agentAt]]
  /\ escrow' = [escrow EXCEPT ![agentAt] = 0]
  /\ payee' = [payee EXCEPT ![agentAt] = NoPayee]
  /\ stamp' = (stamp + 1) % StampCycle
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stampSeen, agentAt>>

Refresh ==
  /\ payee[agentAt] # NoPayee
  /\ stampSeen[agentAt] # stamp
  /\ stampSeen' = [stampSeen EXCEPT ![agentAt] = stamp]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, escrow, payee, stamp, agentAt>>

Return ==
  /\ payee[agentAt] # NoPayee
  /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![agentAt] = @ + escrow[agentAt]]
  /\ escrow' = [escrow EXCEPT ![agentAt] = 0]
  /\ payee' = [payee EXCEPT ![agentAt] = NoPayee]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stampSeen, stamp, agentAt>>

\* The agent never skips a slow participant; it moves on only when escrow clears.
StepOn ==
  /\ payee[agentAt] = NoPayee
  /\ agentAt' = (agentAt + 1) % NumBanks
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, escrow, payee, stampSeen, stamp>>

AgentWork == Post \/ Refresh \/ Return

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Banks, d \in Banks, amt \in Amounts : Originate(b, d, amt)
  \/ AgentWork
  \/ StepOn

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(AgentWork)
  /\ SF_vars(StepOn)

\* Nothing minted, nothing lost: balances plus escrow is a batch-wide constant.
FundsConserved ==
  SumOf(balance, Banks) + SumOf(escrow, Banks) = TotalFunds

EscrowAlwaysClears ==
  \A b \in Banks : (escrow[b] > 0) ~> (escrow[b] = 0)
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumBanks = 3
    TotalFunds = 2
    MaxAmount = 1
    StampCycle = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT FundsConserved

PROPERTY EscrowAlwaysClears
nl:
A national clearing house runs an interbank settlement batch. A fixed amount of settlement money exists on the books at the start of the batch, spread across the participating banks, and the whole point of the batch is that the money only moves -- the clearing house never mints a unit and never lets one evaporate.

Any participant may originate a payment instruction at any time. Originating debits the payer's own balance immediately and parks the amount in that bank's escrow slot, together with a note of which bank is to receive it and a snapshot of the shared settlement ledger's version stamp at the moment the instruction was drawn up. Nothing is locked: this is optimistic. The ledger's version stamp advances every time some payment is actually posted, so a parked instruction that was drawn up before somebody else's posting is now working from a stale snapshot and must not be posted as it stands.

The clearing house drives the batch with a single settlement agent that walks the participants in a fixed cyclic order. The agent works on exactly one participant at a time, and it does not move on to the next participant until the one in front of it has nothing parked in escrow. Participants are known to be slow -- a bank's back office may take a long while to answer -- but no participant is treated as failed, so the agent waits rather than skipping. When the agent is at a participant whose parked instruction carries the current version stamp, it posts the payment: the escrowed amount is credited to the receiving bank, the escrow slot empties, and the ledger's version stamp advances. When the parked instruction carries a stale stamp, the agent refreshes the snapshot to the current stamp and the instruction stays parked for another try. The agent may also give up on a parked instruction and return the escrowed amount to the originator's own balance.

The full action set is: a participant originates a payment instruction, debiting itself into escrow with a version snapshot; the agent posts the current participant's parked instruction when its snapshot is current, crediting the receiver and advancing the version stamp; the agent refreshes a stale snapshot and leaves the instruction parked; the agent returns a parked escrow amount to its originator; and the agent advances to the next participant in the cycle once the current one has an empty escrow slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total settlement money held across all participants' balances plus everything sitting in escrow always equals the amount the batch started with, so no unit of money is created or destroyed by any posting, refresh, return, or origination.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Any amount a participant parks in escrow is eventually cleared out of that escrow slot, either by being posted to its receiver or by being returned to the originator.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m9p5t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumPallets, Robots, MaxEpoch, NetBound

Pallets == 1 .. NumPallets
Epochs == 0 .. MaxEpoch
Mass(p) == p
Orders == [pallet : Pallets, robot : Robots, ep : Epochs]

RECURSIVE Bulk(_)
Bulk(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET p == CHOOSE q \in S : TRUE IN Mass(p) + Bulk(S \ {p})

VARIABLES epoch, assign, air, manifest, cell, believes
vars == <<epoch, assign, air, manifest, cell, believes>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in Epochs
  /\ assign \in [Pallets -> Robots]
  /\ air \subseteq Orders
  /\ manifest \subseteq Pallets
  /\ cell \in 0 .. Bulk(Pallets)
  /\ believes \in [Robots -> Epochs]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ assign \in [Pallets -> Robots]
  /\ air = {}
  /\ manifest = {}
  /\ cell = 0
  /\ believes = [r \in Robots |-> 0]

\* Reconfiguration is epoch-stamped and may move any pallet to any robot.
Reconfigure(f) ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ assign' = f
  /\ UNCHANGED <<air, manifest, cell, believes>>

Issue(p) ==
  /\ LET o == [pallet |-> p, robot |-> assign[p], ep |-> epoch] IN
       /\ o \notin air
       /\ air' = air \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assign, manifest, cell, believes>>

\* The mesh reorders, so a robot's epoch belief only ever moves forward.
AdoptEpoch(o) ==
  /\ o \in air
  /\ o.ep > believes[o.robot]
  /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![o.robot] = o.ep]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assign, air, manifest, cell>>

Discard(o) ==
  /\ o \in air
  /\ air' = air \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assign, manifest, cell, believes>>

\* The chute is the single arbiter: it refuses anything already on its manifest.
Scrap(o) ==
  /\ o \in air
  /\ o.ep >= believes[o.robot]
  /\ o.pallet \notin manifest
  /\ manifest' = manifest \cup {o.pallet}
  /\ cell' = cell + Mass(o.pallet)
  /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![o.robot] = o.ep]
  /\ air' = air \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assign>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in [Pallets -> Robots] : Reconfigure(f)
  \/ \E p \in Pallets : Issue(p)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : AdoptEpoch(o)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Discard(o)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Scrap(o)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AirBound == Cardinality(air) <= NetBound

\* Physical witness: the load cell must account for the manifest exactly.
LoadCellMatchesManifest == cell = Bulk(manifest)
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumPallets = 2
    Robots = {r1, r2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NetBound = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT LoadCellMatchesManifest

CONSTRAINT AirBound
nl:
A warehouse runs a fleet of mobile robots under a single fleet coordinator. The coordinator publishes a configuration that says which robot is responsible for which pallet, and every configuration carries an epoch number. Reconfiguration happens while the floor is live: the coordinator bumps the epoch and republishes a fresh pallet-to-robot assignment, for instance when a robot is pulled off for charging.

The irreversible action in this warehouse is scrapping a pallet down the compaction chute. Once a pallet goes down the chute it is crushed; there is no way to retrieve it, and there is no way to un-scrap it. The chute sits on a load cell that accumulates the total mass it has swallowed, and pallets have different masses, so the load cell reading is an independent physical witness of what has actually gone down. The chute also keeps a manifest listing which pallets it has taken.

Orders travel over the warehouse's radio mesh, which does not preserve order: an order issued under an older epoch can arrive after an order issued under a newer one, and orders can sit in the air for a long time before they land. A robot therefore learns about epochs only from the orders it receives, and its own notion of the current epoch lags the coordinator's. A robot will act on an order whose epoch is at least as new as the epoch the robot itself currently believes in, and acting on an order also advances the robot's belief to that order's epoch. A robot may also simply adopt a newer epoch it hears about in an order addressed to it without acting on that order, and it may discard any order addressed to it. Because two robots can hold orders for the same pallet from two different epochs, the chute manifest is the one shared thing that keeps a pallet from being scrapped twice: the chute refuses a pallet already on its manifest.

The full action set is: the coordinator bumps the epoch and republishes a pallet-to-robot assignment; the coordinator issues a scrap order for a pallet to that pallet's currently assigned robot, stamped with the current epoch; a robot adopts a newer epoch it learns from an order addressed to it; a robot discards an order addressed to it; and a robot presents a pallet to the chute under an order at least as new as the robot's own epoch, whereupon the chute adds the pallet to its manifest and its mass to the load cell.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The chute's load cell reading always equals the total mass of exactly the pallets listed on its manifest, which can only hold if no pallet is ever put down the chute more than once despite reordered orders from different epochs.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m2p5t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, MaxRound

RoundIds == 1 .. MaxRound
Stamps == 0 .. MaxRound
Answers == {"none", "yes", "no"}

VARIABLES round, coord, reply, notices, engraved, journal
vars == <<round, coord, reply, notices, engraved, journal>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in RoundIds
  /\ coord \in {"open", "committed", "aborted"}
  /\ reply \in [Robots -> Answers]
  /\ notices \in [Robots -> SUBSET RoundIds]
  /\ engraved \in [Robots -> Stamps]
  /\ journal \in [Robots -> Stamps]

Init ==
  /\ round = 1
  /\ coord = "aborted"
  /\ reply = [r \in Robots |-> "none"]
  /\ notices = [r \in Robots |-> {}]
  /\ engraved = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
  /\ journal = [r \in Robots |-> 0]

OpenRound ==
  /\ coord # "open"
  /\ round' = (round % MaxRound) + 1
  /\ coord' = "open"
  /\ reply' = [r \in Robots |-> "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<notices, engraved, journal>>

Answer(r, v) ==
  /\ coord = "open"
  /\ reply[r] = "none"
  /\ v \in {"yes", "no"}
  /\ reply' = [reply EXCEPT ![r] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, coord, notices, engraved, journal>>

\* Phase two: a unanimous round pushes one notice per robot into the mesh.
CommitRound ==
  /\ coord = "open"
  /\ \A r \in Robots : reply[r] = "yes"
  /\ coord' = "committed"
  /\ notices' = [r \in Robots |-> notices[r] \cup {round}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, reply, engraved, journal>>

AbortRound ==
  /\ coord = "open"
  /\ \E r \in Robots : reply[r] = "no"
  /\ coord' = "aborted"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, reply, notices, engraved, journal>>

Settle == CommitRound \/ AbortRound

\* Notices sit in an unordered mesh, so k may be an old round's notice acted on
\* after a newer one; the spent-cartridge check is the only thing stopping a
\* second firing, and the stamp wheel keeps only the first round it ever saw.
Fire(r, k) ==
  /\ k \in notices[r]
  /\ engraved[r] = 0
  /\ engraved' = [engraved EXCEPT ![r] = IF engraved[r] = 0 THEN k ELSE engraved[r]]
  /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![r] = k]
  /\ notices' = [notices EXCEPT ![r] = notices[r] \ {k}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, coord, reply>>

DropNotice(r, k) ==
  /\ k \in notices[r]
  /\ notices' = [notices EXCEPT ![r] = notices[r] \ {k}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, coord, reply, engraved, journal>>

AnswerAny == \E r \in Robots, v \in Answers : Answer(r, v)

Next ==
  \/ OpenRound
  \/ AnswerAny
  \/ Settle
  \/ \E r \in Robots, k \in RoundIds : Fire(r, k)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, k \in RoundIds : DropNotice(r, k)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(AnswerAny)
  /\ WF_vars(Settle)

\* Two independent recorders must agree; they diverge exactly on a re-fire.
CartridgeStoryAgrees ==
  \A r \in Robots : engraved[r] = journal[r]

EveryRoundSettles ==
  (coord = "open") ~> (coord # "open")

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2}
    MaxRound = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CartridgeStoryAgrees

PROPERTY EveryRoundSettles
nl:
The same warehouse robot fleet also runs a joint shutdown protocol for damaged aisle gates. Sealing a gate is done with a single-use pyrotechnic cartridge carried by each robot: firing the cartridge welds the gate frame permanently and cannot be undone or repeated, because the cartridge is spent. The cartridge body carries a mechanical stamp wheel that engraves the protocol round number into the metal the very first time the cartridge fires and can never be re-engraved afterwards. Separately, the fleet's maintenance journal records, for each robot, the round number of the most recent firing it saw. The engraving and the journal entry are produced by two different pieces of equipment and are supposed to tell the same story.

The decision to fire is taken by two-phase commit. A coordinator opens a round: it stamps the round with a fresh number and asks every robot to vote. Each robot answers yes or no depending on whether its own gate sensors are happy. If every robot votes yes, the coordinator commits the round and pushes a commit notice out to every robot. If any robot votes no, the coordinator aborts the round and no notices go out at all. Once the round is settled, the coordinator is free to open another round.

Commit notices travel over the same unordered radio mesh the fleet uses for everything else. Notices are not delivered in the order they were sent and they can linger, so a robot can be holding notices from several different rounds at once and may act on them in any order, including acting on an old round's notice long after a newer round's notice arrived. A robot may also throw away a notice it is holding without acting on it. The rule that keeps the fleet honest is that a robot with an already-engraved cartridge refuses to fire again, no matter which notice it is holding.

The full action set is: the coordinator opens a new round and clears the previous votes; a robot answers the open round with a yes or a no; the coordinator commits an all-yes round and pushes a commit notice to every robot; the coordinator aborts a round in which some robot answered no; a robot acts on a commit notice it holds by firing its cartridge, engraving that notice's round on the cartridge and writing that round into the maintenance journal; and a robot throws away a commit notice it holds.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every robot, the round engraved on its cartridge and the round written in the maintenance journal are always the same number, which can only stay true if no robot ever fires its cartridge a second time under a later round's notice.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every round the coordinator opens is eventually settled, that is it eventually reaches either commit or abort.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m2p4t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Blocks, Trains, LongBlocks, ShortRunners

\* Long open-air blocks admit two trains; station-throat blocks admit one.
Cap(b) == IF b \in LongBlocks THEN 2 ELSE 1
Route(t) == IF t \in ShortRunners THEN Blocks \ LongBlocks ELSE Blocks

VARIABLES phase, hold, occ, refused, busy
vars == <<phase, hold, occ, refused, busy>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [Trains -> {"idle", "asking", "running", "abandoned"}]
  /\ hold \in [Blocks -> SUBSET Trains]
  /\ occ \in [Blocks -> SUBSET Trains]
  /\ refused \in [Trains -> SUBSET Blocks]
  /\ busy \in [Blocks -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ phase = [t \in Trains |-> "asking"]
  /\ hold = [b \in Blocks |-> {}]
  /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> {}]
  /\ refused = [t \in Trains |-> {}]
  /\ busy = [b \in Blocks |-> FALSE]

Counted(b) == hold[b] \cup occ[b]

\* A tentative hold consumes a place exactly as real occupancy does.
TakeHold(t, b) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "asking"
  /\ b \in Route(t)
  /\ ~busy[b]
  /\ t \notin Counted(b)
  /\ Cardinality(Counted(b)) < Cap(b)
  /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![b] = hold[b] \cup {t}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, occ, refused, busy>>

Refuse(t, b) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "asking"
  /\ b \in Route(t)
  /\ ~busy[b]
  /\ t \notin Counted(b)
  /\ Cardinality(Counted(b)) >= Cap(b)
  /\ refused' = [refused EXCEPT ![t] = refused[t] \cup {b}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, hold, occ, busy>>

CommitRoute(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "asking"
  /\ \A b \in Route(t) : t \in hold[b]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "running"]
  /\ hold' = [b \in Blocks |-> hold[b] \ {t}]
  /\ occ' = [b \in Blocks |-> IF b \in Route(t) THEN occ[b] \cup {t} ELSE occ[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<refused, busy>>

AbortRoute(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "asking"
  /\ refused[t] # {}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "abandoned"]
  /\ hold' = [b \in Blocks |-> hold[b] \ {t}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, refused, busy>>

ClearOut(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "running"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ occ' = [b \in Blocks |-> occ[b] \ {t}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, refused, busy>>

Reattempt(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] \in {"idle", "abandoned"}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "asking"]
  /\ refused' = [refused EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, occ, busy>>

\* Slow, not failed: an interlocking mid-cycle just does not answer yet.
FlipBusy(b) ==
  /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![b] = ~busy[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, hold, occ, refused>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : TakeHold(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Refuse(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : CommitRoute(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : AbortRoute(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : ClearOut(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : Reattempt(t)
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : FlipBusy(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Holds and occupancy together must fit inside the block's admission limit.
BlockLimitHonoured ==
  \A b \in Blocks : Cardinality(Counted(b)) <= Cap(b)
===========================================================================
nl:
A subway line is divided into signalling blocks, and each block is a physical stretch of track with a hard occupancy limit set by its length and its emergency-braking distance. A short block near a station throat admits only one train; a long open-air block admits two. Exceeding a block's limit is the thing the signalling system exists to prevent.

A train does not enter the line one block at a time. It is granted a whole route at once, and a route may span several blocks, so the grant is arranged as a two-phase commit across the interlockings that own those blocks. In the first phase the train's route controller asks each interlocking on the route to reserve a place. An interlocking that still has room below its block's limit takes a tentative hold on behalf of that train; an interlocking that is already at its limit refuses. Tentative holds count against the block's limit exactly like real occupancy does, because a held place is a place that must be there when the train arrives.

Interlockings are relay-based and can be slow: an interlocking that is mid-cycle simply does not answer for a while. Slow is not the same as failed here -- the route controller does not conclude anything from silence, and it never re-asks a block behind the interlocking's back. It waits. When every interlocking on the route has taken a hold, the route controller commits: each hold on that route turns into real occupancy and the train runs. If any interlocking on the route refuses, the route controller aborts, and every hold that route had taken anywhere is dropped. A train that has finished running clears out of its blocks, and an aborted route may be attempted again from scratch.

The full action set is: an interlocking that is not mid-cycle and still has room takes a tentative hold for a train whose route includes its block; an interlocking that is at its block's limit records a refusal for such a train; the route controller commits a route on which every block has taken a hold, converting all of them to occupancy; the route controller aborts a route on which some block has refused, dropping every hold that route holds; a committed train clears out of all its blocks; an aborted route is put back to idle so it can be attempted again; and an interlocking goes into or comes out of its mid-cycle busy state.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every block, the number of trains counted against it -- tentative holds and real occupancy together -- never exceeds that block's own admission limit.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m4p1t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS QueueDepth, RevisionBudget

NoJob == RevisionBudget + 1
Revisions == 0 .. RevisionBudget

VARIABLES rev, queue, job, journal, quiet
vars == <<rev, queue, job, journal, quiet>>

InHand == IF job = NoJob THEN 0 ELSE 1
Outstanding == Len(queue) + InHand

TypeOK ==
  /\ rev \in Revisions
  /\ queue \in Seq(Revisions)
  /\ Len(queue) <= QueueDepth
  /\ job \in Revisions \cup {NoJob}
  /\ journal \in Seq(Revisions)
  /\ quiet \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ rev = 0
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ job = NoJob
  /\ journal = <<>>
  /\ quiet = FALSE

\* Backpressure: depth limit plus the shift's remaining revision budget.
Submit ==
  /\ Len(queue) < QueueDepth
  /\ rev + Outstanding < RevisionBudget
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, rev)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, job, journal, quiet>>

Take ==
  /\ job = NoJob
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ job' = Head(queue)
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, journal, quiet>>

GoQuiet ==
  /\ ~quiet
  /\ quiet' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, queue, job, journal>>

WakeUp ==
  /\ quiet
  /\ quiet' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, queue, job, journal>>

\* The applier writes base+1, so writing a stale job would reuse a number.
Write ==
  /\ ~quiet
  /\ job # NoJob
  /\ job = rev
  /\ rev' = job + 1
  /\ journal' = Append(journal, job + 1)
  /\ job' = NoJob
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, quiet>>

Rebase ==
  /\ ~quiet
  /\ job # NoJob
  /\ job # rev
  /\ job' = rev
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, queue, journal, quiet>>

WorkStep == Write \/ Rebase

Next == Submit \/ Take \/ GoQuiet \/ WakeUp \/ WorkStep

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(WakeUp)
  /\ WF_vars(Take)
  /\ SF_vars(WorkStep)

\* Log contiguity: position i of the journal strip must hold exactly i.
JournalContiguous ==
  \A i \in 1 .. Len(journal) : journal[i] = i

AdmittedWorkCompletes ==
  \A k \in 1 .. RevisionBudget : (rev + Outstanding >= k) ~> (rev >= k)
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    QueueDepth = 3
    RevisionBudget = 6

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT JournalContiguous

PROPERTY AdmittedWorkCompletes
nl:
A subway line's signalling centre keeps one shared movement-authority record for the line. The record carries a revision number, and every accepted change bumps that revision by exactly one. The centre also keeps a revision journal: an append-only strip that records the revision number produced by each change as it is written. A healthy line produces revisions 1, 2, 3, and so on with no repeats and no gaps in that strip, because each change is supposed to be built on top of the revision immediately before it.

Changes arrive from trackside as authority-update jobs and are held in a bounded staging queue in front of the single applier. The queue has a fixed depth, and that depth is the line's backpressure: when the staging queue is full, trackside submissions are simply not admitted, and the centre also refuses to admit more work than the record's remaining revision budget for the shift. When a job is admitted it records the revision the record showed at the moment of admission -- that is the revision the job was built against.

The applier takes jobs off the front of the queue one at a time. The applier is a relay-driven unit and it can be slow: it goes into a busy sub-cycle during which it does nothing at all, and it comes out again. Slow is not failed here -- it always comes back out, and nothing is ever taken away from it while it is quiet. When the applier is responsive and the job in its hand was built against the record's current revision, it writes the change: the record moves to the job's base revision plus one and that number is stamped on the journal strip. When the job in its hand was built against an older revision, writing it would silently discard whatever landed in between, so instead the applier rebases the job onto the record's current revision and keeps it in hand for another go.

The full action set is: trackside submits a job, which is admitted only when the staging queue is below its depth limit and the shift's revision budget still allows it; the applier takes the front job off the queue into its hand; the applier enters its busy sub-cycle; the applier leaves its busy sub-cycle; the responsive applier writes a job whose base matches the record's current revision, bumping the record and stamping the journal; and the responsive applier rebases a job whose base is older than the record's current revision.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The revision journal strip always reads exactly 1, 2, 3, ... with the entry in position i being the number i, so no write ever reuses or skips a revision number and no accepted change is ever silently overwritten by one built on stale data.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every job admitted into the staging queue is eventually written to the shared record, so the record's revision eventually reaches the count of everything ever admitted.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m1p1t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumDistricts

Controllers == 0 .. (NumDistricts - 1)
Onward(c) == (c + 1) % NumDistricts

VARIABLES baton, plan, sheet, editing, acked, quiet
vars == <<baton, plan, sheet, editing, acked, quiet>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ baton \in Controllers
  /\ plan \subseteq Controllers
  /\ sheet \in [Controllers -> SUBSET Controllers]
  /\ editing \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ acked \in [Controllers -> SUBSET Controllers]
  /\ quiet \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ baton = 0
  /\ plan = {}
  /\ sheet = [c \in Controllers |-> {}]
  /\ editing = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]
  /\ acked = [c \in Controllers |-> {}]
  /\ quiet = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]

\* A working sheet must never survive a handover; that is the whole guard.
PassBaton ==
  /\ ~quiet[baton]
  /\ ~editing[baton]
  /\ baton' = Onward(baton)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, sheet, editing, acked, quiet>>

CopyPlan ==
  /\ ~quiet[baton]
  /\ ~editing[baton]
  /\ sheet' = [sheet EXCEPT ![baton] = plan]
  /\ editing' = [editing EXCEPT ![baton] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, plan, acked, quiet>>

\* Write-back replaces the whole plan with the working sheet plus own feeder.
WriteBack ==
  /\ ~quiet[baton]
  /\ editing[baton]
  /\ plan' = sheet[baton] \cup {baton}
  /\ acked' = [acked EXCEPT ![baton] = {baton}]
  /\ sheet' = [sheet EXCEPT ![baton] = {}]
  /\ editing' = [editing EXCEPT ![baton] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, quiet>>

DiscardSheet ==
  /\ ~quiet[baton]
  /\ editing[baton]
  /\ sheet' = [sheet EXCEPT ![baton] = {}]
  /\ editing' = [editing EXCEPT ![baton] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, plan, acked, quiet>>

Unshed ==
  /\ ~quiet[baton]
  /\ ~editing[baton]
  /\ baton \in plan
  /\ plan' = plan \ {baton}
  /\ acked' = [acked EXCEPT ![baton] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, sheet, editing, quiet>>

GoQuiet(c) ==
  /\ ~quiet[c]
  /\ quiet' = [quiet EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, plan, sheet, editing, acked>>

ComeBack(c) ==
  /\ quiet[c]
  /\ quiet' = [quiet EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, plan, sheet, editing, acked>>

Next ==
  \/ PassBaton
  \/ CopyPlan
  \/ WriteBack
  \/ DiscardSheet
  \/ Unshed
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : GoQuiet(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : ComeBack(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Coverage: nothing a controller was told is on the plan may have fallen off.
AcknowledgedFeedersStillOnPlan ==
  \A c \in Controllers : acked[c] \subseteq plan
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumDistricts = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT AcknowledgedFeedersStillOnPlan
nl:
A regional power grid is protected by a set of load-shedding controllers, one per substation district, that all edit a single shared shed plan. The shed plan is a list of which feeders are currently marked for shedding, and it is the only authoritative copy: there is no per-district version of it. Each controller cares about exactly one feeder, its own, and its job is to get that feeder onto the plan when its district is in trouble and off the plan when the district recovers.

Editing the plan is a read-then-write affair, not a single atomic operation. A controller first copies the plan into a local working sheet, then later writes the working sheet back with its own feeder added. If the plan had moved on between the copy and the write-back -- because some other controller had meanwhile added its own feeder -- writing the old sheet back would quietly erase that other feeder from the plan. That is the lost update this system has to avoid, and it matters physically: a feeder that a controller has been told is on the plan but which has silently fallen off will not actually be shed when the grid needs it.

Editing rights circulate on a ring. A single editing baton travels around the controllers in fixed cyclic order, and only the controller currently holding the baton may copy the plan, write a sheet back, or take its own feeder off the plan. A controller passes the baton onward only when it is not in the middle of an edit, so a working sheet never survives across a baton handover. Controllers are known to be slow: a controller can go quiet for a long stretch while it polls its district's telemetry, and while it is quiet it neither edits nor passes the baton. Nothing ever pulls the baton away from a quiet controller -- the ring treats slowness as slowness, not as failure -- and a quiet controller always comes back. A controller may also give up on a working sheet and throw it away.

Whenever a controller successfully writes its feeder onto the plan, it records an acknowledgement that its feeder is on the plan; when it takes its feeder off the plan it withdraws that acknowledgement.

The full action set is: the baton holder, if not quiet and not mid-edit, passes the baton to the next controller on the ring; the baton holder copies the plan into its working sheet; the baton holder writes its working sheet back with its own feeder added and records the acknowledgement; the baton holder throws away its working sheet; the baton holder takes its own feeder off the plan and withdraws its acknowledgement; a controller goes quiet; and a quiet controller comes back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every feeder that some controller currently holds an acknowledgement for is still on the shared shed plan, so no write-back ever erases a feeder another controller was told had been recorded.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m9p3t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumHolds, NumSlots, EastHolds, MaxEpoch

Holds == 1 .. NumHolds
Slots == 1 .. NumSlots
NoSlot == 0
NoHold == 0
Branches == {"east", "west"}
BranchOf(h) == IF h \in EastHolds THEN "east" ELSE "west"
Epochs == 0 .. MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, slotOf, occupant, placedAt, alive
vars == <<epoch, slotOf, occupant, placedAt, alive>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in Epochs
  /\ slotOf \in [Holds -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ occupant \in [Slots -> Holds \cup {NoHold}]
  /\ placedAt \in [Holds -> Epochs]
  /\ alive \in [Branches -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ slotOf = [h \in Holds |-> NoSlot]
  /\ occupant = [s \in Slots |-> NoHold]
  /\ placedAt = [h \in Holds |-> 0]
  /\ alive = [b \in Branches |-> TRUE]

\* Placement writes both books at once; that pairing is the safety mechanism.
Place(h, s) ==
  /\ alive[BranchOf(h)]
  /\ slotOf[h] = NoSlot
  /\ occupant[s] = NoHold
  /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![h] = s]
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = h]
  /\ placedAt' = [placedAt EXCEPT ![h] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alive>>

Lift(h) ==
  /\ alive[BranchOf(h)]
  /\ slotOf[h] # NoSlot
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![slotOf[h]] = NoHold]
  /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![h] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, placedAt, alive>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOf, occupant, placedAt, alive>>

\* A placement from an earlier epoch no longer matches the shelf arrangement.
LiftStale(h) ==
  /\ alive[BranchOf(h)]
  /\ slotOf[h] # NoSlot
  /\ placedAt[h] < epoch
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![slotOf[h]] = NoHold]
  /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![h] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, placedAt, alive>>

Sweep(h) ==
  /\ ~alive[BranchOf(h)]
  /\ slotOf[h] # NoSlot
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![slotOf[h]] = NoHold]
  /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![h] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, placedAt, alive>>

GoSilent(b) ==
  /\ \A x \in Branches : alive[x]
  /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, slotOf, occupant, placedAt>>

SweepAny == \E h \in Holds : Sweep(h)

Next ==
  \/ \E h \in Holds, s \in Slots : Place(h, s)
  \/ \E h \in Holds : Lift(h)
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E h \in Holds : LiftStale(h)
  \/ SweepAny
  \/ \E b \in Branches : GoSilent(b)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(SweepAny)

\* The two books must be exact inverses of each other on every occupied slot.
ShelfBooksAgree ==
  /\ \A h \in Holds : slotOf[h] # NoSlot => occupant[slotOf[h]] = h
  /\ \A s \in Slots : occupant[s] # NoHold => slotOf[occupant[s]] = s

SilentBranchSlotsReclaimed ==
  \A h \in Holds :
    (slotOf[h] # NoSlot /\ ~alive[BranchOf(h)]) ~> (slotOf[h] = NoSlot)
===========================================================================

CONSTANTS
    NumHolds = 3
    NumSlots = 2
    EastHolds = {1, 2}
    MaxEpoch = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ShelfBooksAgree

PROPERTY SilentBranchSlotsReclaimed
nl:
A public library system runs a reservation service backed by a single hold shelf at the central depot. The shelf has a fixed number of numbered slots, and a patron reservation that has been filled occupies exactly one slot until the patron collects it. Two branch servers, east and west, each handle their own patrons' reservations and place filled reservations onto the shelf.

The shelf layout is not static. Periodically the depot reconfigures it -- reindexing slots after shelving work, or repartitioning capacity between branches -- and each reconfiguration carries a new epoch number. A reservation records the epoch in force when it was placed. After a reconfiguration, a reservation still sitting on a slot from a previous epoch no longer corresponds to the shelf's current arrangement, and the branch that placed it must lift it off and place it again under the current epoch.

Placement is recorded in two independent places: the branch's own reservation record says which slot a reservation went into, and the shelf's slot register says which reservation is sitting in each slot. These two must tell the same story, because the whole point of the slot register is that a slot can hold one reservation and the depot staff go to the slot the reservation record names.

A branch server can crash silently. There is no failure announcement and no last message: the branch simply stops answering, and a crashed branch never comes back and never places or lifts anything again. Slots that a silent branch left occupied would sit dead forever, so the depot runs a sweep that reclaims any slot whose occupying reservation belongs to a branch that has gone silent, clearing both the slot register and that reservation's record together. At most one of the two branches ever goes silent.

The full action set is: a live branch places one of its unplaced reservations into a free slot, recording the current epoch; a live branch lifts one of its own placed reservations off the shelf; the depot bumps the epoch, reconfiguring the shelf; a live branch lifts off one of its reservations that was placed under an older epoch; the depot's sweep reclaims a slot occupied by a reservation belonging to a silent branch; and a branch goes silent.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The branch reservation records and the shelf slot register always agree in both directions -- every reservation that names a slot is the reservation the register shows sitting in that slot, and every occupied slot's reservation names that same slot -- so no slot is ever allocated to two reservations at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every slot left occupied by a reservation belonging to a branch that has gone silent is eventually reclaimed by the depot sweep.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m2p3t5 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumDistricts, NumWindows, Substations

Districts == 1 .. NumDistricts
Windows == 1 .. NumWindows
NoOne == 0
NoWin == 0

VARIABLES register, promised, phase, want, votes
vars == <<register, promised, phase, want, votes>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ register \in [Windows -> Districts \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ promised \in [Districts -> SUBSET Windows]
  /\ phase \in [Districts -> {"idle", "asking", "done", "dropped"}]
  /\ want \in [Districts -> Windows \cup {NoWin}]
  /\ votes \in [Districts -> SUBSET Substations]

Init ==
  /\ register = [w \in Windows |-> NoOne]
  /\ promised = [d \in Districts |-> {}]
  /\ phase = [d \in Districts |-> "idle"]
  /\ want = [d \in Districts |-> NoWin]
  /\ votes = [d \in Districts |-> {}]

OpenRound(d, w) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "idle"
  /\ register[w] = NoOne
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "asking"]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![d] = w]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![d] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<register, promised>>

VoteYes(d, sub) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "asking"
  /\ sub \notin votes[d]
  /\ register[want[d]] = NoOne
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![d] = votes[d] \cup {sub}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<register, promised, phase, want>>

\* Commit writes the register and the district's own list in one step.
CommitRound(d) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "asking"
  /\ votes[d] = Substations
  /\ register[want[d]] = NoOne
  /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![want[d]] = d]
  /\ promised' = [promised EXCEPT ![d] = promised[d] \cup {want[d]}]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<want, votes>>

DropRound(d) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "asking"
  /\ register[want[d]] # NoOne
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "dropped"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<register, promised, want, votes>>

ClearRound(d) ==
  /\ phase[d] \in {"done", "dropped"}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![d] = NoWin]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![d] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<register, promised>>

GiveBack(d, w) ==
  /\ w \in promised[d]
  /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![w] = NoOne]
  /\ promised' = [promised EXCEPT ![d] = promised[d] \ {w}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, want, votes>>

\* The operator's override must strike the window off the loser's list too.
Seize(d, w) ==
  /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![w] = d]
  /\ promised' = [x \in Districts |->
                    IF x = d THEN promised[x] \cup {w} ELSE promised[x] \ {w}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, want, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Districts, w \in Windows : OpenRound(d, w)
  \/ \E d \in Districts, sub \in Substations : VoteYes(d, sub)
  \/ \E d \in Districts : CommitRound(d)
  \/ \E d \in Districts : DropRound(d)
  \/ \E d \in Districts : ClearRound(d)
  \/ \E d \in Districts, w \in Windows : GiveBack(d, w)
  \/ \E d \in Districts, w \in Windows : Seize(d, w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every promise a district is planning against must be backed by the register.
PromisesMatchRegister ==
  \A d \in Districts : \A w \in promised[d] : register[w] = d

CONSTANTS
    NumDistricts = 2
    NumWindows = 2
    Substations = {sub1, sub2}

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT PromisesMatchRegister
nl:
When a regional grid must shed load, it does so in scheduled shed windows: fixed time slots on the rolling-blackout calendar. A shed window can be allocated to exactly one district, because two districts blacking out in the same window would drop more load than the interties can absorb. The control centre keeps a window register saying, for each window, which district holds it. Each district separately keeps its own list of windows it has been promised, and it plans its hospital generators and traffic-signal batteries against that list, so a promise that does not match the register is a real operational hazard.

Allocating a window is agreed by two-phase commit across the region's substations, because every substation has to know the schedule before it takes effect. A district that wants a currently unheld window opens a round and asks the substations; each substation votes yes as long as the window is still unheld when it is asked. When every substation has voted yes and the window is still unheld, the district commits: the register records the window against that district and the district adds the window to its own promised list. If the window turns out to be held by the time the district looks again, the round is abandoned. A district clears a finished round, successful or abandoned, before starting another. A district may also give a window back, clearing it from the register and from its own list.

Above all this sits the grid operator's privileged override. In an emergency the operator can seize a window for a district outright, with no round and no substation votes, and the seizure takes precedence over whatever was there before: the register is rewritten to name the seizing district, and the window is struck off the promised list of whichever district previously held it. The override is the one path that can move a window away from a district that did not agree to give it up.

The full action set is: a district opens a round for an unheld window; a substation votes yes in a district's open round while the wanted window is still unheld; a district whose round has all substation votes and whose wanted window is still unheld commits, writing the register and its own promised list; a district abandons a round whose wanted window has been taken; a district clears a finished round back to idle; a district gives back a window it holds; and the operator seizes a window for a district, rewriting the register and striking the window off the previous holder's list.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every window on any district's promised list is recorded in the control centre's window register as belonging to that same district, so no shed window is ever allocated to two districts at once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m4p5t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS NumBags, MinLanes, MaxLanes

Bags == 1 .. NumBags
Slots == 0 .. NumBags

VARIABLES lanes, line, where, manifest, overprint
vars == <<lanes, line, where, manifest, overprint>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ lanes \in MinLanes .. MaxLanes
  /\ line \in Seq(Bags)
  /\ Len(line) <= lanes
  /\ where \in [Bags -> {"kerb", "line", "container"}]
  /\ manifest \in Seq(Bags)
  /\ overprint \in [Bags -> Slots]

Init ==
  /\ lanes = MinLanes
  /\ line = <<>>
  /\ where = [b \in Bags |-> "kerb"]
  /\ manifest = <<>>
  /\ overprint = [b \in Bags |-> 0]

OpenLane ==
  /\ lanes < MaxLanes
  /\ lanes' = lanes + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<line, where, manifest, overprint>>

\* A lane may only be pulled once the standing line already fits underneath.
CloseLane ==
  /\ lanes > MinLanes
  /\ Len(line) <= lanes - 1
  /\ lanes' = lanes - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<line, where, manifest, overprint>>

\* Backpressure: the kerb is refused whenever the line is at the live limit.
Induct(b) ==
  /\ where[b] = "kerb"
  /\ Len(line) < lanes
  /\ line' = Append(line, b)
  /\ where' = [where EXCEPT ![b] = "line"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lanes, manifest, overprint>>

\* The drop is irreversible; the overprint records the manifest slot taken.
Drop ==
  /\ line # <<>>
  /\ Len(manifest) < NumBags
  /\ manifest' = Append(manifest, Head(line))
  /\ overprint' = [overprint EXCEPT ![Head(line)] = Len(manifest) + 1]
  /\ where' = [where EXCEPT ![Head(line)] = "container"]
  /\ line' = Tail(line)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lanes>>

KickBack ==
  /\ line # <<>>
  /\ where' = [where EXCEPT ![Head(line)] = "kerb"]
  /\ line' = Tail(line)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lanes, manifest, overprint>>

ServeFront == Drop \/ KickBack

Next ==
  \/ OpenLane
  \/ CloseLane
  \/ \E b \in Bags : Induct(b)
  \/ ServeFront

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(ServeFront)

\* Manifest position and tag overprint must tell the same story at every slot.
ManifestSlotsCoherent ==
  \A i \in 1 .. Len(manifest) : overprint[manifest[i]] = i

LineNeverHoldsForever ==
  \A b \in Bags : (where[b] = "line") ~> (where[b] # "line")
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumBags = 4
    MinLanes = 1
    MaxLanes = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ManifestSlotsCoherent

PROPERTY LineNeverHoldsForever
nl:
An airport baggage router feeds bags from the check-in kerb onto a single make-up chute that loads them into an aircraft container. Dropping a bag down the make-up chute is the irreversible step: the bag lands inside the container, the container is on a live loading cycle, and there is no mechanism to lift a bag back out. A bag that went down the chute twice would mean the airline's records show one bag but two things happened to it, which is exactly the fault this router is designed to make impossible.

Between the kerb and the chute sits the induction queue, a physical line of totes on the sorter loop. The queue is served strictly from its front. The queue's depth limit is not fixed: lanes of the sorter loop open and close during the shift as maintenance crews work on them, so the limit rises and falls while bags are moving. When the queue is at its current depth limit, kerb inductions are refused outright -- that is the router's backpressure -- and a lane may only be taken out of service when the queue is short enough to fit under the reduced limit.

Two things can happen to the bag at the front of the queue. It can be dropped down the make-up chute, or the scanner can fail to read its tag, in which case the bag is kicked back out to the kerb to be re-inducted later. Only a bag standing at the kerb may be inducted, and a bag that has already gone down the chute is never at the kerb again, which is what keeps a bag from making a second trip.

Every drop is written to the container's loading manifest, in order, and at the same moment the bag's own baggage tag is overprinted with the manifest position it just took. The manifest and the tag overprints are meant to be a consistent pair of records: the bag written at manifest position i must be carrying an overprint reading i.

The full action set is: a maintenance crew brings a sorter lane back into service, raising the queue's depth limit; a crew takes a lane out of service, lowering the limit, which is only allowed when the queue already fits under the lower limit; a bag standing at the kerb is inducted into the back of the queue when the queue is below its current limit; the bag at the front of the queue is dropped down the make-up chute, appended to the loading manifest, and overprinted with its manifest position; and the bag at the front of the queue is kicked back out to the kerb after a failed tag read.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every position i of the container's loading manifest, the bag recorded at that position carries an overprint reading exactly i, which can only hold if no bag was ever dropped down the make-up chute more than once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: No bag ever sits in the induction queue forever; every bag that is inducted eventually leaves the queue, either down the chute or back out to the kerb.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m7p3t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumNodes, NumSlots, MaxStamp

Nodes == 1 .. NumNodes
Slots == 1 .. NumSlots
Nobody == 0
NoSlot == 0
Stamps == 0 .. MaxStamp

Blank == [slot |-> NoSlot, stamp |-> 0]

VARIABLES reg, snap, slip, shed, quiet
vars == <<reg, snap, slip, shed, quiet>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in [Slots -> [owner : Nodes \cup {Nobody}, stamp : Stamps]]
  /\ snap \in [Nodes -> [slot : Slots \cup {NoSlot}, stamp : Stamps]]
  /\ slip \in [Nodes -> [slot : Slots \cup {NoSlot}, stamp : Stamps]]
  /\ shed \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ quiet \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ reg = [s \in Slots |-> [owner |-> Nobody, stamp |-> 0]]
  /\ snap = [n \in Nodes |-> Blank]
  /\ slip = [n \in Nodes |-> Blank]
  /\ shed = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
  /\ quiet = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]

Snapshot(n, s) ==
  /\ ~quiet[n]
  /\ slip[n].slot = NoSlot
  /\ snap[n].slot = NoSlot
  /\ reg[s].owner = Nobody
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![n] = [slot |-> s, stamp |-> reg[s].stamp]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, slip, shed, quiet>>

\* The swap and the grant slip are written in one indivisible step; that
\* pairing is what stops two nodes from both believing they took the slot.
Swap(n) ==
  /\ ~quiet[n]
  /\ snap[n].slot # NoSlot
  /\ slip[n].slot = NoSlot
  /\ reg[snap[n].slot].owner = Nobody
  /\ reg[snap[n].slot].stamp = snap[n].stamp
  /\ reg[snap[n].slot].stamp < MaxStamp
  /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![snap[n].slot] =
               [owner |-> n, stamp |-> snap[n].stamp + 1]]
  /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![n] =
               [slot |-> snap[n].slot, stamp |-> snap[n].stamp + 1]]
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![n] = Blank]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shed, quiet>>

DropSnapshot(n) ==
  /\ ~quiet[n]
  /\ snap[n].slot # NoSlot
  /\ \/ reg[snap[n].slot].owner # Nobody
     \/ reg[snap[n].slot].stamp # snap[n].stamp
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![n] = Blank]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, slip, shed, quiet>>

DoShed(n) ==
  /\ slip[n].slot # NoSlot
  /\ ~shed[n]
  /\ shed' = [shed EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, snap, slip, quiet>>

GiveBack(n) ==
  /\ ~quiet[n]
  /\ slip[n].slot # NoSlot
  /\ reg[slip[n].slot].stamp = slip[n].stamp
  /\ reg[slip[n].slot].stamp < MaxStamp
  /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![slip[n].slot] =
               [owner |-> Nobody, stamp |-> slip[n].stamp + 1]]
  /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![n] = Blank]
  /\ shed' = [shed EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, quiet>>

\* Quiet is slowness, never failure: nothing is ever reclaimed from a quiet node.
Hush(n) ==
  /\ ~quiet[n]
  /\ quiet' = [quiet EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, snap, slip, shed>>

Rouse(n) ==
  /\ quiet[n]
  /\ quiet' = [quiet EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, snap, slip, shed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Nodes, s \in Slots : Snapshot(n, s)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Swap(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : DropSnapshot(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : DoShed(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : GiveBack(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Hush(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Rouse(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A grant slip must be backed by the register at exactly its stamp.
GrantsBackedByRegister ==
  \A n \in Nodes :
    slip[n].slot # NoSlot =>
      /\ reg[slip[n].slot].owner = n
      /\ reg[slip[n].slot].stamp = slip[n].stamp
==========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumNodes = 2
    NumSlots = 2
    MaxStamp = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT GrantsBackedByRegister
nl:
A power-grid load shedder divides its rolling-blackout schedule into rotation slots. A rotation slot is a chunk of shedding duty, and it may be allocated to only one dispatch node at a time: if two nodes both believed they owned the same rotation slot, both would open their breakers in that window and the grid would lose double the intended load.

Ownership lives in a compare-and-swap register, one per rotation slot. Each register holds two fields: who owns the slot, and a stamp that is bumped every time the register changes hands in either direction. A dispatch node that wants a slot first takes a snapshot of a register it finds unowned, noting the stamp it saw. Later it attempts the swap: the swap goes through only if the register is still unowned and still carries the exact stamp from the snapshot. If either has moved, the attempt is dead and the node throws its snapshot away. A successful swap bumps the stamp and, in the same indivisible step, writes the node's own grant slip recording which slot it took and at which stamp. Giving a slot back is also a compare-and-swap: the node swaps the register back to unowned, again only if the register still carries the stamp on its grant slip, and the stamp bumps once more.

Dispatch nodes are slow. A node may go quiet for a long stretch -- it is polling feeder telemetry, or its link is congested -- and while quiet it takes no snapshots, attempts no swaps, and gives nothing back. Quiet is not failure here: nothing reclaims a slot from a quiet node, and a quiet node always becomes responsive again, so a held slot always comes back on the node's own initiative. This is exactly why a node's snapshot can be arbitrarily old by the time it tries to use it.

While a node holds a slot it may actually perform the shed for that slot, which it does at most once per grant.

The full action set is: a responsive node with no slot in hand snapshots an unowned register and notes its stamp; a responsive node completes a compare-and-swap on a register that still matches its snapshot, taking ownership, bumping the stamp and writing its grant slip; a responsive node throws away a snapshot whose register no longer matches; a node holding a slot performs the shed for it; a responsive node compare-and-swaps its slot back to unowned using the stamp on its grant slip; a node goes quiet; and a quiet node becomes responsive.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a dispatch node is holding a grant slip for a rotation slot, that slot's register names that very node as its owner and carries exactly the stamp written on the slip, so no rotation slot is ever allocated to two nodes at once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m3p1t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS NumCentres, MaxTerm, MaxStrip

Centres == 1 .. NumCentres
NoLeader == 0
Terms == 0 .. MaxTerm

VARIABLES term, chief, inService, strip, sealed, acked
vars == <<term, chief, inService, strip, sealed, acked>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in Terms
  /\ chief \in Centres \cup {NoLeader}
  /\ inService \subseteq Centres
  /\ strip \in Seq(Terms)
  /\ sealed \in Seq(Terms)
  /\ acked \subseteq Centres

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ chief = NoLeader
  /\ inService = Centres
  /\ strip = <<>>
  /\ sealed = <<>>
  /\ acked = {}

\* Failover: each election raises the term and clears standing acknowledgements.
Elect(c) ==
  /\ c \in inService
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ chief' = c
  /\ acked' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inService, strip, sealed>>

DropOut ==
  /\ chief # NoLeader
  /\ chief' = NoLeader
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, inService, strip, sealed, acked>>

AppendAdjustment ==
  /\ chief # NoLeader
  /\ Len(strip) < MaxStrip
  /\ strip' = Append(strip, term)
  /\ acked' = {chief}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, inService, sealed>>

Acknowledge(c) ==
  /\ c \in inService
  /\ c \notin acked
  /\ acked' = acked \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, inService, strip, sealed>>

\* The quorum is taken against whoever is in service right now, not a fixed roll.
Confirm ==
  /\ inService # {}
  /\ 2 * Cardinality(acked \cap inService) > Cardinality(inService)
  /\ Len(strip) > Len(sealed)
  /\ sealed' = strip
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, inService, strip, acked>>

\* A rollback discards the whole provisional tail and stops dead at the
\* sealed copy; nothing inside the sealed copy may ever be undone.
RollBack ==
  /\ Len(strip) > Len(sealed)
  /\ strip' = sealed
  /\ acked' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, inService, sealed>>

BringIn(c) ==
  /\ c \notin inService
  /\ inService' = inService \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, strip, sealed, acked>>

TakeOut(c) ==
  /\ c \in inService
  /\ Cardinality(inService) > 1
  /\ inService' = inService \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, strip, sealed, acked>>

Resolve == Confirm \/ RollBack

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Centres : Elect(c)
  \/ DropOut
  \/ AppendAdjustment
  \/ \E c \in Centres : Acknowledge(c)
  \/ Resolve
  \/ \E c \in Centres : BringIn(c)
  \/ \E c \in Centres : TakeOut(c)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Resolve)

\* The strip must always be an extension of the audit recorder's sealed copy.
StripExtendsSealed ==
  /\ Len(sealed) <= Len(strip)
  /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(sealed) : strip[i] = sealed[i]

ProvisionalWorkResolves ==
  (Len(strip) > Len(sealed)) ~> (Len(strip) = Len(sealed))
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumCentres = 3
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxStrip = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT StripExtendsSealed

PROPERTY ProvisionalWorkResolves
nl:
A metro's signalling estate keeps one shared record of timetable adjustments for the line: an ordered strip of entries, each entry being one adjustment to block headways. The strip is the operational truth, and an adjustment that has been confirmed to the traffic controllers must never afterwards vanish from it or be replaced by a different adjustment at that position. That would be a lost update, and on this railway it means a driver acting on an instruction that the signalling estate no longer believes it gave.

The estate is a cluster of signalling centres. Exactly one centre at a time acts as controlling centre, chosen by an election that carries a term number; each election raises the term. A controlling centre can drop out at any moment -- power event, comms failure -- and when it does the cluster is left with no controlling centre until the next election raises the term again and installs a new one. Membership of the cluster is not fixed: centres are brought into service and taken out of service during the working day, so the number of centres that count towards a decision rises and falls while the line is running.

Only the controlling centre may append an adjustment to the strip, stamping it with the term it is serving under. An appended adjustment is not yet confirmed. Member centres acknowledge the strip as it currently stands, and when the acknowledgements standing from centres that are currently in service form a strict majority of the centres currently in service, the estate confirms the strip: an independent audit recorder takes a sealed copy of everything on the strip up to that point, and that sealed copy is what the traffic controllers are told. Adjustments past the end of the sealed copy are still provisional and the whole provisional tail may be discarded in one go, stopping dead at the sealed copy; adjustments inside the sealed copy may never be rolled back.

The full action set is: an election raises the term and installs an in-service centre as controlling centre; the controlling centre drops out, leaving the estate with none; the controlling centre appends a term-stamped adjustment to the strip and acknowledges it itself; an in-service centre acknowledges the strip as it stands; the estate confirms the strip when in-service acknowledgements form a strict majority of the in-service centres, extending the audit recorder's sealed copy; the whole provisional tail beyond the sealed copy is rolled back off the strip in one go, clearing the standing acknowledgements; a centre is brought into service; and a centre is taken out of service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The strip always extends the audit recorder's sealed copy exactly -- the sealed copy is never longer than the strip and every position inside the sealed copy holds the same adjustment on the strip -- so no confirmed adjustment is ever rolled back or overwritten.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: The strip never carries a provisional adjustment forever; whenever it runs past the sealed copy it eventually comes back into line with it, every provisional adjustment being either confirmed or rolled back.

CONSTANTS NumBays, NumRobots, NorthBays, MinLimit, MaxLimit, DeckSize

Bays == 1 .. NumBays
Robots == 1 .. NumRobots
Nobody == 0
Aisles == {"north", "south"}
AisleOf(b) == IF b \in NorthBays THEN "north" ELSE "south"

vars == <<shelf, deck, aisleHold, bayHold, limit>>

RECURSIVE DeckUpto(_)

  /\ shelf \in [Bays -> 0 .. MaxLimit]
  /\ deck \in [Robots -> 0 .. DeckSize]
  /\ aisleHold \in [Aisles -> Robots \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ bayHold \in [Bays -> Robots \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ limit \in [Bays -> MinLimit .. MaxLimit]
