  /\ shelf = [b \in Bays |-> 1]
  /\ deck = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
  /\ aisleHold = [a \in Aisles |-> Nobody]
  /\ bayHold = [b \in Bays |-> Nobody]
  /\ limit = [b \in Bays |-> MaxLimit]

TakeAisle(r, a) ==
  /\ aisleHold[a] = Nobody
  /\ aisleHold' = [aisleHold EXCEPT ![a] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, deck, bayHold, limit>>

\* Fine hold is only reachable from underneath a coarse hold by the same robot.
TakeBay(r, b) ==
  /\ bayHold[b] = Nobody
  /\ aisleHold[AisleOf(b)] = r
  /\ bayHold' = [bayHold EXCEPT ![b] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, deck, aisleHold, limit>>

Pick(r, b) ==
  /\ bayHold[b] = r
  /\ shelf[b] > 0
  /\ deck[r] < DeckSize
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![b] = shelf[b] - 1]
  /\ deck' = [deck EXCEPT ![r] = deck[r] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleHold, bayHold, limit>>

Place(r, b) ==
  /\ bayHold[b] = r
  /\ deck[r] > 0
  /\ shelf[b] < limit[b]
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![b] = shelf[b] + 1]
  /\ deck' = [deck EXCEPT ![r] = deck[r] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleHold, bayHold, limit>>

\* Rack beams move mid-shift, but never below what is already on the shelf.
Restripe(r, b, c) ==
  /\ bayHold[b] = r
  /\ c \in MinLimit .. MaxLimit
  /\ c >= shelf[b]
  /\ limit' = [limit EXCEPT ![b] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, deck, aisleHold, bayHold>>

DropBay(r, b) ==
  /\ bayHold[b] = r
  /\ bayHold' = [bayHold EXCEPT ![b] = Nobody]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, deck, aisleHold, limit>>

DropAisle(r, a) ==
  /\ aisleHold[a] = r
  /\ \A b \in Bays : AisleOf(b) = a => bayHold[b] # r
  /\ aisleHold' = [aisleHold EXCEPT ![a] = Nobody]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, deck, bayHold, limit>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Robots, a \in Aisles : TakeAisle(r, a)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Bays : TakeBay(r, b)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Bays : Pick(r, b)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Bays : Place(r, b)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Bays, c \in MinLimit .. MaxLimit : Restripe(r, b, c)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Bays : DropBay(r, b)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, a \in Aisles : DropAisle(r, a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Nightly count: shelves plus decks is a building-wide constant.
StockCountHolds ==
  ShelfUpto(NumBays) + DeckUpto(NumRobots) = NumBays
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumBays = 3
    NumRobots = 2
    NorthBays = {1, 2}
    MinLimit = 1
    MaxLimit = 2
    DeckSize = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT StockCountHolds
nl:
A goods-to-person warehouse stores loose stock units in numbered bays, and the bays are grouped into aisles. A fleet of robots shuttles stock units between bays. Every stock unit in the building is either sitting in a bay or riding on a robot; the building neither manufactures units nor swallows them, and the nightly count has to come out at the same number it came in at.

Working on a bay requires two levels of exclusive hold, coarse before fine. A robot must first take hold of the aisle a bay belongs to, and only then may it take hold of the bay itself. An aisle or a bay is held by at most one robot. A robot lets go of a bay when it has finished with it, and lets go of an aisle only once it is holding no bays inside that aisle.

A robot holding a bay may pick one stock unit off the shelf onto its own deck, provided the bay is not empty and the robot's deck is not already full, or it may place one stock unit from its deck onto the shelf, provided the bay is below its current shelf limit.

Shelf limits are not fixed. Rack beams get moved during the shift, so a bay's limit can be raised or lowered while the building is running. Only the robot holding a bay may restripe it, and a restripe may never set a limit below the number of units already sitting in that bay -- a lower limit would leave stock with nowhere to be, and the units would have to go somewhere the count cannot see.

The full action set is: a robot takes hold of a free aisle; a robot takes hold of a free bay inside an aisle it already holds; a robot picks one unit off a held bay onto its deck; a robot places one unit from its deck into a held bay below that bay's limit; a robot restripes a held bay to a new limit that is not below the bay's current contents; a robot lets go of a bay; and a robot lets go of an aisle in which it holds no bays.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of stock units sitting in bays plus the number riding on robot decks always equals the total the building started the shift with, so no pick, place or restripe ever creates or destroys a unit.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m4p6t5 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS NumDrones, NumSorties, QueueDepth, MaxClearance

Drones == 1 .. NumDrones
Sorties == 1 .. NumSorties
Grounded == 0
Clearances == 0 .. MaxClearance

VARIABLES queue, flying, cred, roster, clearance, filed
vars == <<queue, flying, cred, roster, clearance, filed>>

Queued(s) == \E i \in 1 .. Len(queue) : queue[i] = s
Current(d) == d \in roster /\ cred[d] = clearance

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(Sorties)
  /\ Len(queue) <= QueueDepth
  /\ flying \in [Sorties -> Drones \cup {Grounded}]
  /\ cred \in [Drones -> Clearances]
  /\ roster \subseteq Drones
  /\ clearance \in Clearances
  /\ filed \subseteq Sorties

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ flying = [s \in Sorties |-> Grounded]
  /\ cred = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ roster = Drones
  /\ clearance = 0
  /\ filed = {}

\* Backpressure: a full dispatch queue simply refuses the fire model.
Generate(s) ==
  /\ Len(queue) < QueueDepth
  /\ s \notin filed
  /\ ~Queued(s)
  /\ flying[s] = Grounded
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, s)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<flying, cred, roster, clearance, filed>>

\* Authorization is checked at hand-off and again at completion.
HandOff(d) ==
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ Current(d)
  /\ \A s \in Sorties : flying[s] # d
  /\ flying' = [flying EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = d]
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, roster, clearance, filed>>

ReportDone(s) ==
  /\ flying[s] # Grounded
  /\ Current(flying[s])
  /\ flying' = [flying EXCEPT ![s] = Grounded]
  /\ filed' = filed \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cred, roster, clearance>>

\* A rotation makes every outstanding credential stale at once.
Rotate ==
  /\ clearance < MaxClearance
  /\ clearance' = clearance + 1
  /\ flying' = [s \in Sorties |-> Grounded]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cred, roster, filed>>

Reissue(d) ==
  /\ d \in roster
  /\ cred[d] < clearance
  /\ cred' = [cred EXCEPT ![d] = clearance]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, flying, roster, clearance, filed>>

Ground(d) ==
  /\ d \in roster
  /\ roster' = roster \ {d}
  /\ flying' = [s \in Sorties |-> IF flying[s] = d THEN Grounded ELSE flying[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cred, clearance, filed>>

Authorize(d) ==
  /\ d \notin roster
  /\ roster' = roster \cup {d}
  /\ cred' = [cred EXCEPT ![d] = clearance]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, flying, clearance, filed>>

ReissueAny == \E d \in Drones : Reissue(d)

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Sorties : Generate(s)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : HandOff(d)
  \/ \E s \in Sorties : ReportDone(s)
  \/ Rotate
  \/ ReissueAny
  \/ \E d \in Drones : Ground(d)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : Authorize(d)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(ReissueAny)

\* Nothing stale or off-roster may be in the air.
OnlyCurrentDronesFly ==
  \A s \in Sorties : flying[s] # Grounded => Current(flying[s])

StaleCredentialsResolved ==
  \A d \in Drones :
    (d \in roster /\ cred[d] < clearance) ~> (d \notin roster \/ cred[d] = clearance)
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumDrones = 2
    NumSorties = 2
    QueueDepth = 2
    MaxClearance = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT OnlyCurrentDronesFly

PROPERTY StaleCredentialsResolved
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm flies camera drones over an active fire front. Sorties are generated by the fire behaviour model and are held in a bounded dispatch queue at the ground station; the queue has a fixed depth and, when it is full, newly generated sorties are simply not admitted, which is the station's backpressure against a runaway fire model.

Flying over an active fire requires a live airspace clearance. The incident air controller publishes a clearance and every drone carries a credential stamped with the clearance it was issued against. Clearances are rotated -- when manned tankers enter the box, when the wind shifts, when a temporary flight restriction changes shape -- and rotating the clearance instantly makes every outstanding credential stale. A drone carrying a stale credential is not authorized: it must not be flying, and anything it was flying is dropped back to the fire model to be regenerated. A drone that is on the authorized roster can pull a fresh credential for the current clearance.

The incident commander holds a privileged override over the roster. The commander can ground a drone outright, which strikes it from the roster and immediately drops whatever sortie it was flying, and the commander can authorize a drone directly, putting it on the roster with a credential for the current clearance without waiting for the normal issuing cycle. Grounding takes effect at once and does not care what the drone was doing.

A sortie at the front of the dispatch queue is handed to a drone only if that drone is on the roster, carries a credential matching the current clearance, and is not already flying something. The drone flies it and reports it complete, and reporting complete likewise requires that the drone is still on the roster and still carries a current credential at that moment.

The full action set is: the fire model puts a fresh sortie into the dispatch queue when the queue is below its depth; the front sortie is handed to a rostered drone carrying a current credential; a flying drone that is still rostered and current reports its sortie complete; the air controller rotates the clearance, which drops every sortie currently being flown; a rostered drone pulls a fresh credential for the current clearance; the commander grounds a drone, striking it from the roster and dropping its sortie; and the commander authorizes a drone onto the roster with a current credential.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any sortie that is currently being flown is being flown by a drone that is on the authorized roster and whose credential matches the clearance now in force, so no grounded drone and no drone holding a stale credential is ever in the air.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every rostered drone left holding a stale credential eventually stops being in that position, either by pulling a fresh credential for the current clearance or by being grounded off the roster.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m0p4t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumLevels, NumFirms, DeepLevels, MaxStamp

Levels == 1 .. NumLevels
Firms == 1 .. NumFirms
NoLevel == 0
Stamps == 0 .. MaxStamp

\* Deep levels around the indicative price hold two orders; thin levels one.
Bound(p) == IF p \in DeepLevels THEN 2 ELSE 1

VARIABLES resting, stamp, reading, seen, live
vars == <<resting, stamp, reading, seen, live>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ resting \in [Levels -> 0 .. 2]
  /\ stamp \in [Levels -> Stamps]
  /\ reading \in [Firms -> Levels \cup {NoLevel}]
  /\ seen \in [Firms -> Stamps]
  /\ live \in [Firms -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ resting = [p \in Levels |-> 0]
  /\ stamp = [p \in Levels |-> 0]
  /\ reading = [f \in Firms |-> NoLevel]
  /\ seen = [f \in Firms |-> 0]
  /\ live = [f \in Firms |-> TRUE]

ReadLevel(f, p) ==
  /\ live[f]
  /\ reading[f] = NoLevel
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![f] = p]
  /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![f] = stamp[p]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<resting, stamp, live>>

\* Acceptance checks the stamp and the room against the level as it stands now.
Accept(f) ==
  /\ live[f]
  /\ reading[f] # NoLevel
  /\ stamp[reading[f]] = seen[f]
  /\ resting[reading[f]] < Bound(reading[f])
  /\ stamp[reading[f]] < MaxStamp
  /\ resting' = [resting EXCEPT ![reading[f]] = resting[reading[f]] + 1]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![reading[f]] = stamp[reading[f]] + 1]
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![f] = NoLevel]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seen, live>>

Reread(f) ==
  /\ live[f]
  /\ reading[f] # NoLevel
  /\ stamp[reading[f]] # seen[f]
  /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![f] = stamp[reading[f]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<resting, stamp, reading, live>>

GiveUp(f) ==
  /\ live[f]
  /\ reading[f] # NoLevel
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![f] = NoLevel]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<resting, stamp, seen, live>>

Pull(p) ==
  /\ resting[p] > 0
  /\ stamp[p] < MaxStamp
  /\ resting' = [resting EXCEPT ![p] = resting[p] - 1]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![p] = stamp[p] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reading, seen, live>>

\* Silent crash: no notice at all, and at most one firm ever goes quiet.
Crash(f) ==
  /\ \A g \in Firms : live[g]
  /\ live' = [live EXCEPT ![f] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<resting, stamp, reading, seen>>

SweepDangling(f) ==
  /\ ~live[f]
  /\ reading[f] # NoLevel
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![f] = NoLevel]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<resting, stamp, seen, live>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Firms, p \in Levels : ReadLevel(f, p)
  \/ \E f \in Firms : Accept(f)
  \/ \E f \in Firms : Reread(f)
  \/ \E f \in Firms : GiveUp(f)
  \/ \E p \in Levels : Pull(p)
  \/ \E f \in Firms : Crash(f)
  \/ \E f \in Firms : SweepDangling(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The opening cross array must never be over-filled at any price level.
LevelBoundHonoured ==
  \A p \in Levels : resting[p] <= Bound(p)
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumLevels = 2
    NumFirms = 2
    DeepLevels = {1}
    MaxStamp = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT LevelBoundHonoured
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction. During the auction the book is organised by price level, and each price level admits only a bounded number of resting orders: the deep levels around the indicative opening price take two resting orders, the thin outer levels take one. The bound is not advisory. The matching engine's opening cross allocates against a fixed-size array per level, and a level that ever carried more resting orders than its bound would corrupt the cross.

Member firms submit into the book optimistically, without ever taking a lock on a price level. A firm first reads a level, noting the level's current change stamp. It then submits: the submission is accepted only if the level's change stamp is still exactly what the firm read. If the stamp has moved -- because some other firm got in first, or because an order was pulled -- the submission is rejected and the firm re-reads the level and keeps its intention alive for another attempt. A firm may also simply give up on an intention. Every accepted submission and every pulled order bumps the level's change stamp. The room check happens at the moment of acceptance against the level as it stands then, not against what the firm read earlier.

One member firm can crash silently during the auction. There is no disconnect message and no cancel-on-disconnect notice; the firm just stops, and it never submits, retries, or gives up again. A firm that crashes while holding a live reading leaves that reading dangling, and the exchange's auction supervisor sweeps dangling readings belonging to firms that have gone quiet. At most one firm crashes during the auction.

The full action set is: a live firm with no intention in hand reads a price level and notes its change stamp; a live firm's submission is accepted when the level's stamp still matches its reading and the level still has room, adding a resting order and bumping the stamp; a live firm whose reading is out of date re-reads the level and keeps its intention; a live firm gives up an intention; an order is pulled off a level, freeing a place and bumping the stamp; a firm crashes silently; and the supervisor sweeps the dangling reading of a firm that has gone quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No price level ever carries more resting orders than that level's own bound, even when several firms are submitting against readings taken before each other's submissions landed.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m0p2t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumMachines, TotalCoins, BagLimit, MaxStamp

Machines == 1 .. NumMachines
Stamps == 0 .. MaxStamp

VARIABLES vault, hopper, bag, mark, ledger
vars == <<vault, hopper, bag, mark, ledger>>

RECURSIVE Held(_)
Held(k) == IF k = 0 THEN 0 ELSE hopper[k] + bag[k] + Held(k - 1)

TypeOK ==
  /\ vault \in 0 .. TotalCoins
  /\ hopper \in [Machines -> 0 .. TotalCoins]
  /\ bag \in [Machines -> 0 .. BagLimit]
  /\ mark \in [Machines -> Stamps]
  /\ ledger \in Stamps

Init ==
  /\ vault = TotalCoins
  /\ hopper = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ bag = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ mark = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ ledger = 0

\* Sealing is optimistic: the machine copies the stamp it last saw, no locking.
Seal(m, k) ==
  /\ bag[m] = 0
  /\ k \in 1 .. BagLimit
  /\ hopper[m] >= k
  /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![m] = hopper[m] - k]
  /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![m] = k]
  /\ mark' = [mark EXCEPT ![m] = ledger]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, ledger>>

\* Bags arrive in any order; only a bag whose stamp still matches books in.
BookIn(m) ==
  /\ bag[m] > 0
  /\ mark[m] = ledger
  /\ ledger < MaxStamp
  /\ vault' = vault + bag[m]
  /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
  /\ ledger' = ledger + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hopper, mark>>

Restamp(m) ==
  /\ bag[m] > 0
  /\ mark[m] # ledger
  /\ mark' = [mark EXCEPT ![m] = ledger]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, hopper, bag, ledger>>

Recall(m) ==
  /\ bag[m] > 0
  /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![m] = hopper[m] + bag[m]]
  /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, mark, ledger>>

Refill(m, k) ==
  /\ k \in 1 .. BagLimit
  /\ vault >= k
  /\ vault' = vault - k
  /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![m] = hopper[m] + k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bag, mark, ledger>>

RestampAny == \E m \in Machines : Restamp(m)

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines, k \in 1 .. BagLimit : Seal(m, k)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : BookIn(m)
  \/ RestampAny
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Recall(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines, k \in 1 .. BagLimit : Refill(m, k)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(RestampAny)

\* Vault plus hoppers plus bags is the network's unchanging cash total.
CoinsConserved ==
  vault + Held(NumMachines) = TotalCoins

StaleBagsGetRestamped ==
  \A m \in Machines :
    (bag[m] > 0 /\ mark[m] # ledger) ~> (bag[m] = 0 \/ mark[m] = ledger)
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumMachines = 2
    TotalCoins = 4
    BagLimit = 2
    MaxStamp = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CoinsConserved

PROPERTY StaleBagsGetRestamped
nl:
An operator runs a network of vending machines backed by a single central cash vault. Every coin in the business is at any moment in exactly one of three places: sitting in a machine's hopper, riding in a sealed courier bag on its way to the vault, or lying in the vault itself. Coins are not minted and not lost, and the operator's daily reconciliation depends on that being literally true.

A machine sends cash in by sealing a bag: coins leave its hopper and go into the bag, and the bag is stamped with the vault ledger's change stamp as the machine last saw it. This is deliberately optimistic -- the machine takes no lock on the ledger and does not wait for the vault's permission to seal a bag.

Courier bags do not arrive in the order they were sealed. Routes differ, vans break down, and the vault takes whichever bag is in front of it. When the vault picks up a bag whose stamp matches the ledger's current stamp, it books the bag in: the coins land in the vault and the ledger's stamp moves on. When the vault picks up a bag whose stamp is out of date -- because some other machine's bag was booked in first -- it cannot book it in as it stands, so it restamps the bag with the ledger's current stamp and the bag waits for another attempt. The operator may also recall a bag, sending its coins straight back to the machine's hopper. Separately, the operator refills a machine's hopper with change drawn from the vault.

The full action set is: a machine seals coins from its hopper into a courier bag stamped with the ledger's current stamp; the vault books in a bag whose stamp matches the ledger, moving the coins into the vault and advancing the stamp; the vault restamps a bag whose stamp is out of date, leaving the coins in the bag; a bag is recalled and its coins returned to the machine's hopper; and the operator moves change from the vault into a machine's hopper.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The coins in the vault, the coins in every machine hopper and the coins in every courier bag always add up to exactly the amount of cash the network started with, so no sealing, booking, restamping, recall or refill ever creates or destroys a coin.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: A courier bag never stays out of date forever; every bag carrying a stale stamp is eventually either restamped to the ledger's current stamp or emptied back to its machine.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m1p3t5 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumControllers, NumSidings, MaxLap

Controllers == 1 .. NumControllers
Sidings == 1 .. NumSidings
Unheld == 0
Laps == 0 .. MaxLap
NextOnRing(c) == (c % NumControllers) + 1

VARIABLES baton, lap, lapBook, register, keyed
vars == <<baton, lap, lapBook, register, keyed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ baton \in Controllers
  /\ lap \in Laps
  /\ lapBook \in [Laps -> Controllers \cup {Unheld}]
  /\ register \in [Sidings -> [owner : Controllers \cup {Unheld}, lap : Laps]]
  /\ keyed \in [Sidings -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ baton = 1
  /\ lap = 0
  /\ lapBook = [l \in Laps |-> IF l = 0 THEN 1 ELSE Unheld]
  /\ register = [s \in Sidings |-> [owner |-> Unheld, lap |-> 0]]
  /\ keyed = [s \in Sidings |-> FALSE]

\* Each handover opens a lap and is written into the lap book straight away.
PassBaton ==
  /\ lap < MaxLap
  /\ baton' = NextOnRing(baton)
  /\ lap' = lap + 1
  /\ lapBook' = [lapBook EXCEPT ![lap + 1] = NextOnRing(baton)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<register, keyed>>

Allocate(s) ==
  /\ register[s].owner = Unheld
  /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![s] = [owner |-> baton, lap |-> lap]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, lap, lapBook, keyed>>

KeyLock(s) ==
  /\ register[s].owner = baton
  /\ ~keyed[s]
  /\ keyed' = [keyed EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, lap, lapBook, register>>

UnkeyLock(s) ==
  /\ register[s].owner = baton
  /\ keyed[s]
  /\ keyed' = [keyed EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, lap, lapBook, register>>

GiveBack(s) ==
  /\ register[s].owner = baton
  /\ ~keyed[s]
  /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![s] = [owner |-> Unheld, lap |-> 0]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, lap, lapBook, keyed>>

\* The override opens its own lap so the seizure is still auditable.
Seize(s, c) ==
  /\ lap < MaxLap
  /\ lap' = lap + 1
  /\ lapBook' = [lapBook EXCEPT ![lap + 1] = c]
  /\ baton' = c
  /\ keyed' = [keyed EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
  /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![s] = [owner |-> c, lap |-> lap + 1]]

ForceFree(s) ==
  /\ register[s].owner # Unheld
  /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![s] = [owner |-> Unheld, lap |-> 0]]
  /\ keyed' = [keyed EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, lap, lapBook>>

Next ==
  \/ PassBaton
  \/ \E s \in Sidings : Allocate(s)
  \/ \E s \in Sidings : KeyLock(s)
  \/ \E s \in Sidings : UnkeyLock(s)
  \/ \E s \in Sidings : GiveBack(s)
  \/ \E s \in Sidings, c \in Controllers : Seize(s, c)
  \/ \E s \in Sidings : ForceFree(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Provenance: every live allocation traces back to the lap book.
AllocationsTraceToLapBook ==
  \A s \in Sidings :
    register[s].owner # Unheld => lapBook[register[s].lap] = register[s].owner
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumControllers = 3
    NumSidings = 2
    MaxLap = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT AllocationsTraceToLapBook
nl:
At the terminus of a metro line there are a small number of turnback sidings, and a siding is a slot that exactly one incoming service may be allocated at a time. Several area controllers share responsibility for the terminus, and any of them may allocate a siding, so the terminus needs a rule about who is entitled to allocate at any given moment.

The rule is a circulating baton. The baton moves around the controllers in a fixed cyclic order, and each handover starts a new lap. The terminus keeps a lap book: an ordered record that writes down, for every lap number, which controller was holding the baton during that lap. Only the controller currently holding the baton may allocate a free siding, and when it does, the siding's register entry records both the allocating controller and the lap number in force at that moment. The controller holding the baton may also key the physical lock on a siding it has allocated, unkey it again, and give a siding back, which clears the register entry. A siding that is keyed cannot be given back until it is unkeyed.

Above all this sits the duty controller's privileged override. In a disruption the duty controller can seize a siding for any controller at all: the seizure starts a fresh lap, writes that controller into the lap book for the new lap, hands the baton to that controller, unkeys the siding and rewrites the register entry to that controller at the new lap, regardless of who held the siding before. The duty controller can also force a siding free outright, unkeying it and clearing its register entry no matter whose it was.

The point of writing the lap number into the register is that every live allocation can be audited back to the lap book: an allocation claiming lap n must have been made by the controller the lap book shows holding the baton during lap n.

The full action set is: the baton is passed to the next controller on the ring, starting a new lap and writing that controller into the lap book; the baton holder allocates a free siding, recording itself and the current lap in the register; the baton holder keys the lock on a siding it holds; the baton holder unkeys a siding it holds; the baton holder gives back an unkeyed siding it holds, clearing the register; the duty controller seizes a siding for a controller, starting a new lap, writing the lap book, handing over the baton, unkeying the siding and rewriting the register; and the duty controller forces a siding free, unkeying it and clearing the register.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every siding whose register entry names an owner names a controller that the lap book shows was holding the baton during the lap recorded in that same entry, so no siding is ever allocated by a controller that was not entitled to allocate, and no siding carries two live allocations.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m2p3t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumStations, NumBays, NumCars

Stations == 1 .. NumStations
Bays == 1 .. NumBays
Cars == 1 .. NumCars
NoCar == 0
NoBay == 0

VARIABLES booked, phase, wants, midCycle, gone
vars == <<booked, phase, wants, midCycle, gone>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ booked \in [Stations -> [Bays -> Cars \cup {NoCar}]]
  /\ phase \in [Cars -> {"waiting", "asking", "running", "balked"}]
  /\ wants \in [Cars -> Bays \cup {NoBay}]
  /\ midCycle \in [Stations -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ gone \subseteq Cars

Init ==
  /\ booked = [st \in Stations |-> [b \in Bays |-> NoCar]]
  /\ phase = [c \in Cars |-> "waiting"]
  /\ wants = [c \in Cars |-> NoBay]
  /\ midCycle = [st \in Stations |-> FALSE]
  /\ gone = {}

DropBookings(c) ==
  [st \in Stations |->
     [b \in Bays |-> IF booked[st][b] = c THEN NoCar ELSE booked[st][b]]]

NameBay(c, b) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "waiting"
  /\ c \notin gone
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "asking"]
  /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![c] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, midCycle, gone>>

\* Each station books into its own plan; nothing is ever booked on its behalf.
Book(st, c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "asking"
  /\ ~midCycle[st]
  /\ booked[st][wants[c]] = NoCar
  /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![st][wants[c]] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, wants, midCycle, gone>>

\* The controller only ever proceeds on unanimity across the whole line.
StartRun(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "asking"
  /\ \A st \in Stations : booked[st][wants[c]] = c
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "running"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, wants, midCycle, gone>>

Balk(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "asking"
  /\ \E st \in Stations : booked[st][wants[c]] \notin {NoCar, c}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "balked"]
  /\ booked' = DropBookings(c)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wants, midCycle, gone>>

BackToWaiting(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "balked"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "waiting"]
  /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![c] = NoBay]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, midCycle, gone>>

LeaveSite(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "running"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "waiting"]
  /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![c] = NoBay]
  /\ booked' = DropBookings(c)
  /\ gone' = gone \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<midCycle>>

FlipCycle(st) ==
  /\ midCycle' = [midCycle EXCEPT ![st] = ~midCycle[st]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, phase, wants, gone>>

LeaveAny == \E c \in Cars : LeaveSite(c)

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars, b \in Bays : NameBay(c, b)
  \/ \E st \in Stations, c \in Cars : Book(st, c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : StartRun(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Balk(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : BackToWaiting(c)
  \/ LeaveAny
  \/ \E st \in Stations : FlipCycle(st)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(LeaveAny)

\* Unanimity holds for the whole run, not merely at the moment of commit.
RunningCarOwnsItsBayEverywhere ==
  \A c \in Cars :
    phase[c] = "running" =>
      /\ wants[c] # NoBay
      /\ \A st \in Stations : booked[st][wants[c]] = c

EveryRunEnds ==
  \A c \in Cars : (phase[c] = "running") ~> (phase[c] # "running")
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumStations = 2
    NumBays = 2
    NumCars = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT RunningCarOwnsItsBayEverywhere

PROPERTY EveryRunEnds
nl:
A car-wash site runs a conveyor line that ends in a row of numbered drying bays. A drying bay is a slot: one vehicle at a time occupies it for the whole of its drying cycle, and two vehicles sent to the same bay would collide on the conveyor exit.

A vehicle is not simply pushed into a bay. Before a vehicle may run, every station along the line -- the prewash arch, the foam arch, the rinse arch -- has to have booked that bay for that vehicle in its own local plan, because each station has to set its nozzles and timing for the bay the car is heading to. So the grant is a two-phase commit. A waiting vehicle names the bay it wants and starts asking. Each station, when it is not mid-cycle, books that bay for that vehicle in its own plan, provided the station has not already booked that bay for somebody else. When every station on the line has the bay booked for the same vehicle, the site controller commits and the vehicle runs. If the vehicle finds that some station has that bay booked for a different vehicle, it balks: it gives up on the attempt and all the bookings it did manage to get are dropped. A balked vehicle goes back to waiting and may name a bay again.

Stations are slow. An arch that is mid-cycle simply does not book anything for a while. Slowness is not failure here: no station is ever declared dead, nothing is booked on a station's behalf, and a mid-cycle arch always comes back and books eventually. The site controller never proceeds on partial agreement, no matter how long a station takes.

A vehicle that has run is pushed off the end of the conveyor: its drying cycle finishes, all of its bookings across every station are dropped, and it leaves the site for good rather than queueing again.

The full action set is: a waiting vehicle that has not yet been through names a bay and starts asking; a station that is not mid-cycle books the asked-for bay for an asking vehicle, provided that station has that bay free in its plan; the controller commits a vehicle whose asked-for bay is booked for it at every station, and the vehicle runs; an asking vehicle balks because some station has its bay booked for another vehicle, dropping all of its own bookings; a balked vehicle returns to waiting; a running vehicle finishes its cycle, drops all its bookings and leaves the site; and a station enters or leaves its mid-cycle state.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every vehicle that is running has a bay named, and at every single station on the line that bay is booked for that very vehicle, so no drying bay is ever allocated to two vehicles at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every vehicle that starts running eventually stops running, finishing its drying cycle and freeing its bay.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m7p1t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumSchedulers, MaxRevision

Schedulers == 1 .. NumSchedulers
Revisions == 0 .. MaxRevision
Written == 1 .. MaxRevision
Unwritten == 0

VARIABLES revision, builtOn, noted, inHand, live
vars == <<revision, builtOn, noted, inHand, live>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ revision \in Revisions
  /\ builtOn \in [Written -> Revisions]
  /\ noted \in [Schedulers -> Revisions]
  /\ inHand \in [Schedulers -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ live \in [Schedulers -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ revision = 0
  /\ builtOn = [v \in Written |-> Unwritten]
  /\ noted = [p \in Schedulers |-> 0]
  /\ inHand = [p \in Schedulers |-> FALSE]
  /\ live = [p \in Schedulers |-> TRUE]

ReadList(p) ==
  /\ live[p]
  /\ ~inHand[p]
  /\ noted' = [noted EXCEPT ![p] = revision]
  /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, builtOn, live>>

\* The swap goes through only against the exact revision the scheduler noted,
\* and it records that revision as the new one's ancestor.
Swap(p) ==
  /\ live[p]
  /\ inHand[p]
  /\ noted[p] = revision
  /\ revision < MaxRevision
  /\ revision' = revision + 1
  /\ builtOn' = [builtOn EXCEPT ![revision + 1] = noted[p]]
  /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<noted, live>>

Refresh(p) ==
  /\ live[p]
  /\ inHand[p]
  /\ noted[p] # revision
  /\ noted' = [noted EXCEPT ![p] = revision]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, builtOn, inHand, live>>

Abandon(p) ==
  /\ live[p]
  /\ inHand[p]
  /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, builtOn, noted, live>>

\* A silent crash: no message, and at most one terminal ever goes quiet.
CrashOut(p) ==
  /\ \A q \in Schedulers : live[q]
  /\ live' = [live EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, builtOn, noted, inHand>>

SweepNote(p) ==
  /\ ~live[p]
  /\ inHand[p]
  /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, builtOn, noted, live>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Schedulers : ReadList(p)
  \/ \E p \in Schedulers : Swap(p)
  \/ \E p \in Schedulers : Refresh(p)
  \/ \E p \in Schedulers : Abandon(p)
  \/ \E p \in Schedulers : CrashOut(p)
  \/ \E p \in Schedulers : SweepNote(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every revision reached must name its immediate predecessor as ancestor.
RevisionChainUnbroken ==
  \A v \in Written : v <= revision => builtOn[v] = v - 1
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumSchedulers = 3
    MaxRevision = 4

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT RevisionChainUnbroken
nl:
A hospital keeps one master theatre list: a single shared record holding the day's operating-room schedule. Several schedulers -- the surgical coordinator, the anaesthetics desk -- revise it during the day. The record carries a revision number, and alongside it the hospital keeps a provenance strip: for every revision the record has ever reached, the strip records which revision that one was built on top of.

Revising is a read-modify-write, and there are no locks anywhere. A scheduler first reads the record, noting the revision number it saw, and then works out its change offline -- ringing a surgeon, checking a bed. When it is ready it attempts a compare-and-swap: the change is written only if the record's revision number is still exactly the one the scheduler noted. If somebody else revised the list in the meantime the swap does not go through, because writing the change as it stands would silently discard whatever that other person did. A scheduler in that position may refresh its noted revision to the record's current one and carry on preparing, or it may abandon the change entirely.

Every swap that does go through bumps the revision number by one and writes into the provenance strip the revision the scheduler had noted. A healthy list therefore has a provenance strip in which revision 1 was built on revision 0, revision 2 on revision 1, and so on with no revision ever grafted onto an older ancestor.

One scheduler can crash silently. There is no error, no message, no handover: the terminal simply stops, and that scheduler never reads, refreshes, swaps or abandons again. A scheduler that crashes while holding a noted revision leaves it dangling, and the hospital's records office sweeps dangling notes belonging to schedulers that have gone silent. At most one scheduler crashes during the day.

The full action set is: a live scheduler with nothing in hand reads the record and notes its revision; a live scheduler whose noted revision still matches the record swaps its change in, bumping the revision and writing the provenance strip; a live scheduler whose noted revision is out of date refreshes it to the record's current revision; a live scheduler abandons what it had in hand; a scheduler crashes silently; and the records office sweeps the dangling note of a scheduler that has gone silent.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry on the provenance strip shows that revision as having been built on the revision immediately before it, so no accepted change was ever grafted onto a stale ancestor and no revision of the theatre list was ever silently overwritten.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m3p6t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumCranes, NumCabins, MaxTerm

Cranes == 1 .. NumCranes
Cabins == 1 .. NumCabins
NoBoss == 0
Terms == 1 .. MaxTerm
Resting == 0
OrderSet == [crane : Cranes, term : Terms]

VARIABLES term, boss, orders, stamp, motion, wired
vars == <<term, boss, orders, stamp, motion, wired>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in Terms
  /\ boss \in Cabins \cup {NoBoss}
  /\ orders \subseteq OrderSet
  /\ stamp \in [Cranes -> Terms]
  /\ motion \in [Cranes -> Terms \cup {Resting}]
  /\ wired \in [Cabins -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ term = 1
  /\ boss = NoBoss
  /\ orders = {}
  /\ stamp = [c \in Cranes |-> 1]
  /\ motion = [c \in Cranes |-> Resting]
  /\ wired = [k \in Cabins |-> TRUE]

\* An incoming controller always starts from a stopped, order-free yard.
Elect(k) ==
  /\ wired[k]
  /\ term' = (term % MaxTerm) + 1
  /\ boss' = k
  /\ orders' = {}
  /\ motion' = [c \in Cranes |-> Resting]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, wired>>

\* Silent failure: the cranes are told nothing at all, and only one cabin dies.
CabinDies(k) ==
  /\ boss = k
  /\ \A j \in Cabins : wired[j]
  /\ wired' = [wired EXCEPT ![k] = FALSE]
  /\ boss' = NoBoss
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, orders, stamp, motion>>

Restamp(c) ==
  /\ stamp[c] # term
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![c] = term]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, boss, orders, motion, wired>>

IssueOrder(c) ==
  /\ boss # NoBoss
  /\ [crane |-> c, term |-> term] \notin orders
  /\ orders' = orders \cup {[crane |-> c, term |-> term]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, boss, stamp, motion, wired>>

\* One move at a time in the yard, and only on a current order and stamp.
TakeUp(o) ==
  /\ o \in orders
  /\ o.term = term
  /\ stamp[o.crane] = term
  /\ \A d \in Cranes : motion[d] = Resting
  /\ motion' = [motion EXCEPT ![o.crane] = term]
  /\ orders' = orders \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, boss, stamp, wired>>

ComeToRest(c) ==
  /\ motion[c] # Resting
  /\ motion' = [motion EXCEPT ![c] = Resting]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, boss, orders, stamp, wired>>

CancelOrder(o) ==
  /\ o \in orders
  /\ orders' = orders \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, boss, stamp, motion, wired>>

RestAny == \E c \in Cranes : ComeToRest(c)

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Cabins : Elect(k)
  \/ \E k \in Cabins : CabinDies(k)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : Restamp(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : IssueOrder(c)
  \/ \E o \in OrderSet : TakeUp(o)
  \/ RestAny
  \/ \E o \in OrderSet : CancelOrder(o)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(RestAny)

\* Nothing moves except under the sitting term, with a matching crane stamp.
NoStaleCraneMoves ==
  \A c \in Cranes :
    motion[c] # Resting => (motion[c] = term /\ stamp[c] = term)

EveryMoveComesToRest ==
  \A c \in Cranes : (motion[c] # Resting) ~> (motion[c] = Resting)
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumCranes = 2
    NumCabins = 2
    MaxTerm = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoStaleCraneMoves

PROPERTY EveryMoveComesToRest
nl:
A container terminal moves boxes with a row of yard cranes under a single yard controller. Two controller cabins are wired to the yard, but only one is in charge at a time, and the one in charge is chosen by an election that carries a term number. Every election installs a controller, moves the yard on to a new term, cancels every outstanding move order, and halts whatever the cranes are doing, so an incoming controller always starts from a stopped yard.

A controller can crash silently. There is no alarm and no handover: the cabin simply stops driving the yard, and the cranes get no notification at all. Only one of the two cabins ever fails this way; the other is always available to be elected.

Each crane carries a term stamp of its own, the last term it was told about, and a crane only regards itself as current when its stamp equals the yard's term. A crane can be brought up to date at any time by taking the yard's current term as its stamp. Move orders issued by the sitting controller are stamped with the term in force when they were issued and sit in the yard's order set until they are taken up or cancelled.

A crane picks up a move order only if the order's term is the yard's current term, the crane's own stamp is the current term, and no other crane in the yard is moving -- the terminal runs one crane move at a time so that spreaders never cross. Taking the order up removes it from the order set and puts the crane in motion under that term. A crane in motion completes its move and comes to rest. Orders may also be cancelled without being taken up.

The full action set is: an available cabin is elected, moving the yard to a new term, taking charge, cancelling all outstanding orders and halting every crane; the sitting controller crashes silently, leaving the yard with nobody in charge; a crane takes the yard's current term as its own stamp; the sitting controller issues a term-stamped move order for a crane; a crane with a current stamp takes up an order of the current term while no other crane is moving; a crane in motion completes its move; and an outstanding order is cancelled.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any crane that is in motion is moving under the yard's current term and carries the current term as its own stamp, so no crane ever acts on an order from a superseded term and no crane acts while carrying a stale term stamp.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every crane that starts moving eventually comes to rest.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m1p2t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumSites, NumUnits

Sites == 1 .. NumSites
Units == 1 .. NumUnits
Nowhere == 0
Onward(s) == (s % NumSites) + 1

VARIABLES baton, fridge, onRoad, note, bench
vars == <<baton, fridge, onRoad, note, bench>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ baton \in Sites
  /\ fridge \in [Sites -> SUBSET Units]
  /\ onRoad \subseteq Units
  /\ note \in [Units -> Sites \cup {Nowhere}]
  /\ bench \subseteq Units

Init ==
  /\ baton = 1
  /\ fridge = [s \in Sites |-> IF s = 1 THEN Units ELSE {}]
  /\ onRoad = {}
  /\ note = [u \in Units |-> Nowhere]
  /\ bench = {}

\* The baton only moves on once the holder's bench is clear.
PassBaton ==
  /\ bench = {}
  /\ baton' = Onward(baton)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, onRoad, note, bench>>

Ship(u, d) ==
  /\ u \in fridge[baton]
  /\ d # baton
  /\ fridge' = [fridge EXCEPT ![baton] = fridge[baton] \ {u}]
  /\ onRoad' = onRoad \cup {u}
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![u] = d]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, bench>>

Reroute(u, d) ==
  /\ u \in onRoad
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![u] = d]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, fridge, onRoad, bench>>

\* Boxes turn up in any order; the holder takes whichever one names it.
TakeDelivery(u) ==
  /\ u \in onRoad
  /\ note[u] = baton
  /\ onRoad' = onRoad \ {u}
  /\ fridge' = [fridge EXCEPT ![baton] = fridge[baton] \cup {u}]
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![u] = Nowhere]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, bench>>

ToBench(u) ==
  /\ u \in fridge[baton]
  /\ fridge' = [fridge EXCEPT ![baton] = fridge[baton] \ {u}]
  /\ bench' = bench \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, onRoad, note>>

BackToFridge(u) ==
  /\ u \in bench
  /\ bench' = bench \ {u}
  /\ fridge' = [fridge EXCEPT ![baton] = fridge[baton] \cup {u}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, onRoad, note>>

Next ==
  \/ PassBaton
  \/ \E u \in Units, d \in Sites : Ship(u, d)
  \/ \E u \in Units, d \in Sites : Reroute(u, d)
  \/ \E u \in Units : TakeDelivery(u)
  \/ \E u \in Units : ToBench(u)
  \/ \E u \in Units : BackToFridge(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Stored == UNION {fridge[s] : s \in Sites}

\* Exactly one custody per barcode: no duplicates anywhere, nothing missing.
EveryUnitInOneCustody ==
  /\ \A s \in Sites : \A t \in Sites :
       s # t => fridge[s] \cap fridge[t] = {}
  /\ \A s \in Sites : fridge[s] \cap (onRoad \cup bench) = {}
  /\ onRoad \cap bench = {}
  /\ Stored \cup onRoad \cup bench = Units
===========================================================================

CONSTANTS
    NumSites = 3
    NumUnits = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT EveryUnitInOneCustody
nl:
A regional blood bank tracks individual units of packed red cells by barcode across several hospital sites. Every unit that exists is, at any moment, in exactly one of three custodies: sitting in some site's fridge, riding in a sealed courier box between sites, or lying out on the crossmatch bench. A barcode that appeared in two custodies at once, or that appeared in none, would mean the bank has either invented a unit of blood or lost one, and both are reportable incidents.

Custody changes are written into one shared inventory ledger, and the right to write into that ledger circulates. A single write baton passes around the sites in a fixed cyclic order, and only the site currently holding the baton may move a unit out of its own fridge, take delivery of a unit, or work at the crossmatch bench. A site hands the baton on only once its crossmatch bench is clear, so no unit is ever left out on the bench of a site that has stopped writing.

Courier boxes do not arrive in the order they were sealed. A unit shipped out carries a transfer note naming its destination site, and the destination takes delivery whenever it next holds the baton, in whatever order boxes happen to turn up at its door. A box in transit may also be rerouted, its transfer note rewritten to name a different destination while the unit is still on the road. What never changes is the custody arithmetic: a unit leaving a fridge into a box has left the fridge and is in the box, a unit taken out of a box is in the receiving fridge, and a unit on the bench came out of the baton holder's own fridge.

The full action set is: the baton is passed to the next site on the ring, which is only allowed when the current holder's crossmatch bench is clear; the baton holder ships a unit out of its own fridge into a courier box with a transfer note naming a destination; a courier box already on the road is rerouted, its transfer note rewritten to a different destination; the baton holder takes delivery of a unit whose transfer note names it, moving the unit from the box into its own fridge; the baton holder moves a unit from its own fridge out onto the crossmatch bench; and the baton holder returns a unit from the crossmatch bench to its own fridge.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every barcoded unit is in exactly one custody at all times -- in one and only one site's fridge, or in a courier box, or on the crossmatch bench -- so no unit is ever duplicated across two custodies and no unit ever drops out of the bank's accounting.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m3p5t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumSections, NumStraps, NumCentres, MaxTerm, MaxAllowance

Sections == 1 .. NumSections
Straps == 1 .. NumStraps
Centres == 1 .. NumCentres
NoStrap == 0
NoChief == 0
Terms == 1 .. MaxTerm

VARIABLES term, chief, store, clamped, isolated, allowance
vars == <<term, chief, store, clamped, isolated, allowance>>

Earthed == {s \in Sections : clamped[s] # NoStrap}

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in Terms
  /\ chief \in Centres \cup {NoChief}
  /\ store \subseteq Straps
  /\ clamped \in [Sections -> Straps \cup {NoStrap}]
  /\ isolated \subseteq Sections
  /\ allowance \in 0 .. MaxAllowance

Init ==
  /\ term = 1
  /\ chief = NoChief
  /\ store = Straps
  /\ clamped = [s \in Sections |-> NoStrap]
  /\ isolated = {}
  /\ allowance = 1

Elect(c) ==
  /\ term' = (term % MaxTerm) + 1
  /\ chief' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<store, clamped, isolated, allowance>>

ChiefFails ==
  /\ chief # NoChief
  /\ chief' = NoChief
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, store, clamped, isolated, allowance>>

Isolate(s) ==
  /\ s \notin isolated
  /\ isolated' = isolated \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, store, clamped, allowance>>

\* Earthing is one-way: the strap leaves the store and stays on the section.
Earth(s, k) ==
  /\ chief # NoChief
  /\ s \in isolated
  /\ clamped[s] = NoStrap
  /\ k \in store
  /\ Cardinality(Earthed) < allowance
  /\ store' = store \ {k}
  /\ clamped' = [clamped EXCEPT ![s] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, isolated, allowance>>

PutBackInCircuit(s) ==
  /\ s \in isolated
  /\ clamped[s] = NoStrap
  /\ isolated' = isolated \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, store, clamped, allowance>>

\* The allowance moves during the day but never below what is already earthed.
Adjust(a) ==
  /\ a >= Cardinality(Earthed)
  /\ allowance' = a
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, store, clamped, isolated>>

ElectAny == \E c \in Centres : Elect(c)

Next ==
  \/ ElectAny
  \/ ChiefFails
  \/ \E s \in Sections : Isolate(s)
  \/ \E s \in Sections, k \in Straps : Earth(s, k)
  \/ \E s \in Sections : PutBackInCircuit(s)
  \/ \E a \in 0 .. MaxAllowance : Adjust(a)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(ElectAny)

\* Every serialised strap is in the store or on exactly one section, never lost.

  /\ \A s \in Sections : clamped[s] # NoStrap => clamped[s] \notin store
  /\ \A k \in Straps : k \in store \/ \E s \in Sections : clamped[s] = k

nl:
A metro's traction supply is divided into sections, and the estate's one irreversible action is earthing a section: the section is isolated, a portable earthing strap is clamped across it, and from that moment the section is dead until a depot crew comes out with paperwork to remove the strap by hand. Nothing in the signalling estate can undo an earthing, and a section that somehow got earthed twice would mean a second strap had been clamped on top of a first one that nobody could then account for.

Earthing straps are the estate's physical currency for this. Each strap carries its own serial number and lives in the traction store when it is not in use. Clamping a strap takes it out of the store and puts it on exactly one section. The estate's audit rule is simple: at any moment every strap in the estate is either lying in the traction store or hanging on one section, and never both and never neither.

Authorising an earthing is the job of the controlling centre. Which centre is controlling is decided by an election carrying a term number, and each election installs a centre and moves the estate on to the next term. A controlling centre can fail, leaving the estate with nobody in charge and no earthings possible until an election installs a replacement. Elections can be run at any time, so a failure is always recoverable.

How many sections may stand earthed at once is not a fixed number. It is the traction allowance, and it is adjusted during the day as the depot changes how much of the line it needs alive for stock movements. The allowance may be raised freely, but it may never be set below the number of sections already standing earthed, since straps already clamped cannot be recalled.

A section must be isolated before it can be earthed, and a section that is isolated but not yet earthed can be put back in circuit.

The full action set is: a centre is elected, moving the estate to the next term and taking charge; the controlling centre fails, leaving the estate with nobody in charge; a section is isolated; an isolated section that is not already earthed is earthed by the controlling centre, taking a strap out of the store and clamping it on that section, which is only permitted while fewer sections stand earthed than the current traction allowance; an isolated section that is not earthed is put back in circuit; and the traction allowance is adjusted to any value not below the number of sections already earthed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every earthing strap in the estate is at all times either lying in the traction store or clamped on a section, never both and never unaccounted for, which can only hold if no section is ever earthed a second time on top of a strap already clamped there.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: The estate is never left without a controlling centre forever; whenever the controlling centre fails, an election eventually installs a replacement.

CONSTANTS NumScripts, NumPositions, QueueDepth

Scripts == 1 .. NumScripts
Positions == 1 .. NumPositions
NoPosition == 0

VARIABLES queue, inService, occupied, window, stage
vars == <<queue, inService, occupied, window, stage>>

Spare == inService \ occupied

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(Scripts)
  /\ Len(queue) <= QueueDepth
  /\ inService \subseteq Positions
  /\ occupied \subseteq Positions
  /\ window \in [Scripts -> Positions \cup {NoPosition}]
  /\ stage \in [Scripts -> {"counter", "waiting", "filled", "handed"}]

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ inService = Positions
  /\ occupied = {}
  /\ window = [sc \in Scripts |-> NoPosition]
  /\ stage = [sc \in Scripts |-> "counter"]

\* Backpressure comes from both the queue depth and the live carousel room.
Accept(sc) ==
  /\ stage[sc] = "counter"
  /\ Len(queue) < QueueDepth
  /\ Spare # {}
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, sc)
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![sc] = "waiting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inService, occupied, window>>

Fill(p) ==
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ p \in Spare
  /\ occupied' = occupied \cup {p}
  /\ window' = [window EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = p]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = "filled"]
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inService>>

HandOver(sc) ==
  /\ stage[sc] = "filled"
  /\ occupied' = occupied \ {window[sc]}
  /\ window' = [window EXCEPT ![sc] = NoPosition]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![sc] = "handed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inService>>

BringIntoService(p) ==
  /\ p \notin inService
  /\ inService' = inService \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, occupied, window, stage>>

\* Capacity may only shrink over positions that are actually empty.
TakeOutOfService(p) ==
  /\ p \in inService
  /\ p \notin occupied
  /\ inService' = inService \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, occupied, window, stage>>

RePresent(sc) ==
  /\ stage[sc] = "handed"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![sc] = "counter"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inService, occupied, window>>

Next ==
  \/ \E sc \in Scripts : Accept(sc)
  \/ \E p \in Positions : Fill(p)
  \/ \E sc \in Scripts : HandOver(sc)
  \/ \E p \in Positions : BringIntoService(p)
  \/ \E p \in Positions : TakeOutOfService(p)
  \/ \E sc \in Scripts : RePresent(sc)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Occupancy has to sit inside whatever is in service at that moment.
CarouselFitsLiveCapacity ==
  /\ occupied \subseteq inService
  /\ \A sc \in Scripts : stage[sc] = "filled" => window[sc] \in occupied

nl:
A pharmacy's robotic dispenser fills prescriptions and drops each finished pack into a numbered position on a collection carousel. A position holds one pack: the patient's label is stuck to the carousel window, and staff go to that window to hand the pack over.

Not every position on the carousel is in service. Positions are taken out of service during the day for cleaning, for a jammed shutter, or because a fridge line is being swapped in, and they are brought back into service afterwards. So the carousel's real capacity moves while the pharmacy is open. A position may only be taken out of service if it is empty; a position with a pack sitting in it stays in service until the pack has been handed over.

Prescriptions arrive faster than the robot fills them, so they wait in a bounded work queue in front of the dispensing head. The queue is served from the front and it has a fixed depth. A new prescription is accepted into the queue only if the queue is below its depth and there is at least one in-service position on the carousel that is currently empty; otherwise the pharmacy's counter refuses to take it, which is the dispenser's backpressure against a full carousel and a full queue.

When the robot fills the prescription at the front of the queue it drops the pack into some in-service position that is currently empty, and it records which position that prescription went to so the counter staff can find it. Handing a pack over to a patient empties that position again and clears the record. A prescription that has been handed over can be re-presented later as a fresh prescription.

The full action set is: a prescription is accepted into the back of the queue when the queue is below its depth and some in-service position is empty; the robot fills the prescription at the front of the queue into an empty in-service position, recording the position against that prescription; a pack is handed over to the patient, emptying its position and clearing the record; a position is brought into service; a position that is empty is taken out of service; and a handed-over prescription is re-presented as fresh.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every occupied carousel position is a position that is currently in service, and every filled prescription's recorded position is one of the occupied positions, so the carousel never holds more packs than its in-service positions can carry.
